title: Fiona the Cincinnati Zoo hippo dies at 9 after swallowing a knitted hat
content: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s hippo, died at age nine after swallowing a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure. Born prematurely at 13 kg, she attracted worldwide attention and became an internet sensation that captured millions of hearts.
summary: Fiona, a 9-year-old hippo at Cincinnati Zoo, died after swallowing a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure. She was born prematurely, weighed only 13kg at birth, and became an internet sensation.
author: France 24

title: World This Week with Gavin Lee features four foreign correspondents
content: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.
summary: World This Week is hosted by Gavin Lee. The show includes a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.
author: France 24

title: French parliament adopts controversial police shooting law
content: French senators gave final approval on Friday to controversial legislation granting police officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when using firearms, fulfilling a long-standing demand of the far right even as weeks of student-led protests have thrust the issue of police brutality back into the spotlight. Left-wing lawmakers have vowed to challenge the bill before France's Constitutional Council.
summary: French senators gave final approval on Friday to a law that presumes police officers act in legitimate self‑defence when using firearms. Left‑wing lawmakers plan to challenge the bill before France's Constitutional Council.
author: France 24

title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster RTB, heightening diplomatic tensions
content:
Tensions have risen between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry banned the Burkinabe broadcaster RTB. The ban comes amid a diplomatic dispute involving gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya.

In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, fighting broke out between Congolese forces and the Rwanda‑backed FRN group despite existing peace commitments.

Separately, an Ethiopian entrepreneur is confronting period poverty by working to break menstrual stigma and increase the availability of reusable sanitary pads.
summary: Guinea’s capital Conakry banned the Burkinabe broadcaster RTB amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. The ban has increased tensions between Guinea and Burkina Faso.
author: France 24

title: Paris Court Sentences Three Police Officers Over 2020 Beating of Michel Zecler
content: A Paris court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, a rare ruling. The assault, captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
summary: A Paris court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time for the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, a rare ruling. The assault, captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
author: France 24

title: Putin Proposes Evacuation of Kostiantynivka Civilians as Humanitarian Ceasefire
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. Experts caution that the proposal may serve military rather than humanitarian purposes, prompting debate over how Kyiv should respond.
summary: Russian President Putin suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. Experts warn that the proposal could serve military rather than humanitarian aims.
author: DW World

title: At least 135 Iranian lawyers face repression, UN warns trial rights at risk
content: Repression against Iranian lawyers has risen sharply. Over the past year, at least 135 lawyers in Iran have faced repressive measures. UN experts warn that these actions seriously jeopardize the right of those accused to a trial in a constitutional court.
summary: At least 135 lawyers in Iran have been subjected to repressive measures over the past year. UN experts warn the repression seriously jeopardizes the right of those accused to a trial in a constitutional court.
author: DW World

title: Russian ornithologist Sofia Rosenfeld sentenced to 3.5 years for Navalny foundation donations
content:
Sofia Rosenfeld, a Russian ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds, was sentenced by a Russian court to 3.5 years in a penal colony for making donations to Navalny’s foundation.

Friends and family are campaigning for her release.
summary: Sofia Rosenfeld, an Arctic bird researcher, was sentenced by a Russian court to 3.5 years in a penal colony for donating to Navalny's foundation. Her friends and family are campaigning for her release.
author: DW World

title: COP31: Europe, Africa, Latin America, Pacific nations demand stronger deal in Antalya
content: A coalition of countries representing Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has formally challenged the draft COP31 agreement, calling for explicit measures on fossil‑fuel use and for stronger climate‑finance provisions. The summit in Antalya is set to conclude on Friday, and activists have warned that the negotiations risk collapse. Negotiators continue to seek a consensus that could be endorsed by nearly 200 governments as the final day of talks approaches.
summary: COP31: Europe, Africa, Latin America, Pacific nations demand stronger deal in Antalya.
author: UN News

title: World Food Programme needs $12.1 bn to aid 91 million in 2027 as hunger crisis deepens
content: The World Food Programme (WFP) plans to assist 91 million people in 2027. To achieve that, the agency says it will need $12.1 billion for the next year’s operations. WFP officials warned that funding shortfalls could leave millions more hungry and that another global food crisis is looming.
summary: The World Food Programme says it will require $12.1 billion to assist 91 million people in 2027. It warned that funding shortfalls could leave millions more hungry as another global food crisis looms.
author: UN News

title: UNICEF warns record child casualties as Ukraine faces deadliest year for children
content: Amid the ruins of a twice‑bombed Kyiv kindergarten where a day‑long power cut persisted, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) warned on Friday that Ukrainian children face heightened danger during another harsh winter, noting that child casualty numbers have risen to record levels.
summary: UNICEF highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine as child casualty numbers rise to record levels. The agency cited a twice‑bombed Kyiv kindergarten with a day‑long power cut, leaving playgrounds shattered and classrooms freezing.
author: UN News

title: Record 400+ settler attacks damage West Bank olive harvest, UN urges protection
content: UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs reported on Friday that Israeli settlers carried out more than 400 attacks during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, causing casualties and property damage – a number exceeding any previous season. The United Nations has called on Israel to protect the farmers.
summary: Israeli settlers carried out more than 400 attacks that caused casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said the attacks were the most in any season and urged Israel to protect the farmers.
author: UN News

title: UN General Assembly President visits Rohingya camps after court rules Myanmar committed genocide
content: A day after the United Nations’ top court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. During the visit, the President urged the international community to translate the landmark judgment into concrete action.
summary: A day after the UN’s highest court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. The president urged the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.
author: UN News

title: Eight injured as driver repeatedly rams car into Palestinians in Kafr Qasim
content:
Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel. Footage shared on social media shows the car accelerating toward the victims, all Palestinians, before hitting them and driving away. According to the Times of Israel, three of the injured were in moderate condition and several were women leaving a nearby wedding.

Arab members of parliament have responded by accusing politicians of fuelling hostility, linking the incident to broader tensions in the area.
summary: Eight people were injured when a driver repeatedly rammed his car into Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel. Three of the injured were in moderate condition and several were women leaving a nearby wedding, according to the Times of Israel.
author: Guardian World

title: ICJ finds Myanmar first nation guilty of genocide, revives 1948 convention relevance
content: Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states. In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.
summary: The International Court of Justice ruled by a nine‑to‑six vote that Myanmar is the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide. The judges also issued a detailed roadmap for applying the 1948 genocide convention, including guidance on assessing intent.
author: Guardian World

title: Al-Qadisiyah University removal of male professors sparks protests by up to 400 women
content:
Al‑Qadisiyah University in southern Iraq removed male professors who taught female students, a decision that has drawn criticism from activists who say the move signals a slide toward Taliban‑style gender segregation. The action has sparked protests.

Over the past two weeks, an estimated 400 women have joined demonstrations demanding the return of the displaced professors, a development that appears to have surprised the university’s administrators.
summary: Al-Qadisiyah University in southern Iraq removed male professors teaching female students, a move activists described as a Taliban‑like gender segregation policy. About as many as 400 women have protested over the past two weeks, demanding the professors’ return and surprising university administrators.
author: Guardian World

title: Denmark to expel Russian defence attache over alleged Moscow role in rapper attack
content:
Denmark’s foreign minister, Lars Løkke Rasmussen, announced that the Russian defence attaché in Copenhagen will be expelled after authorities suspected Moscow of being behind an attempted killing of US‑Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner before a concert in Denmark.  

Rasmussen said the Russian ambassador was summoned to the ministry of foreign affairs and informed of the government’s decision.  The expulsion is scheduled to take place within seven days.
summary: Denmark’s foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen will be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of US‑Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner. He added that the Russian ambassador was summoned and the expulsion will take place within seven days.
author: Guardian World

title: Andy Burnham urges closer EU ties, cites 0.5% growth boost, challenges Tories, Reform
content:
Prime Minister challenges rivals to rebuff a plan that he says could add 0.5 % annual growth to the economy and offer hope to young people.  

In a brief statement about future UK‑EU relations, Andy Burnham said, “The important point is that the Britain of today and the EU of today is not the one of 2016,” adding that “Life has moved on in so many ways.”  

Burnham’s political gamble on closer ties with Brussels hinges on the assumption that most British voters share that view.
summary: Prime Minister challenges rivals to reject a plan that Andy Burnham says could add 0.5% annual growth to the economy and give young people hope. Burnham argues that today’s Britain and EU differ from 2016 and frames his push for closer ties as a gamble that depends on voter sentiment.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain releases US activist James “Fergie” Chambers on bail as police raid Dublin home
content:
Spain released pro‑Palestinian donor James “Fergie” Chambers on bail while a court in Spain considers a U.S. extradition request. The release comes amid a series of events linked to the Trump administration’s effort to bring Chambers before U.S. authorities.

At the same time, Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, following a request from U.S. officials. The raid was part of the same extradition case.

Chambers’ case is the first known instance in which the United States has sought to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas. The extradition request is tied to an international money‑laundering charge in the criminal complaint and to donations made to organizations that aid Palestinians in Gaza.
summary: Spain released pro-Palestinian donor James “Fergie” Chambers on bail while a court reviews a US extradition request tied to alleged Hamas support. Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner Stella Schnabel on a US request.
author: Guardian World

title: Three French police officers convicted of racist assault on music producer Michel Zecler
content:
Three French police officers were convicted this month of intentional, racist violence after beating Michel Zecler, a black music producer, in 2020. The officers said Zecler was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic when they assaulted him. The attack was recorded by security cameras in Zecler’s building and later sparked public outrage over police brutality in France.

Zecler, now 47, was the focus of a trial that observers described as a turning point for the recognition of racist violence. The conviction marks the first time the three officers have been found guilty of such conduct in connection with the 2020 beating.
summary: Three French police officers were found guilty of intentional racist violence for beating black music producer Michel Zecler in 2020 after accusing him of not wearing a face mask. The assault, captured on security cameras in his building, sparked outrage in France and the trial was seen as a turning point for recognizing racist violence.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump threatens huge penalties for US tech firms building overseas datacenters
content:
President Donald Trump warned on Friday that he would impose “tremendous penalties” on American technology firms that construct data centers abroad, though he offered no specifics and said he had not yet briefed his own officials about the proposal. The remark was made during a wide‑ranging press conference in the White House briefing room, where Trump also asserted that he has “fantastic relationships” with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

In the same briefing, Trump said he would “look into” a report that Iran might be planning to detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington, D.C., and he expressed support for JD Vance in response to Vice President Kamala Harris’s comments linking Republican midterm losses to the Iran conflict.
summary: Trump threatens huge penalties for US tech firms building overseas datacenters.
author: Guardian World

title: SpaceX Starfactory tour reveals 1M sq ft facility producing Starship rockets
content:
On November 13, SpaceX invited media personnel to tour its Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, following the Starship Flight 15 mission. The five-story facility spans approximately 1 million square feet, with operations divided between the production of Starship’s Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, alongside nearly 330,000 square feet of office space. SpaceX officials describe the design as resembling an automotive manufacturing plant rather than a typical aerospace production site. The tour provided a behind-the-scenes look at the production scale, including a view of a nose cone with windows cut out, which appeared to be a prototype or final article for NASA’s Artemis lunar lander.

Inside the facility, visitors observed giant stainless-steel rocket parts at various subassembly stations, including Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections, and booster components. The quantity of hardware was significant, with rows of nose cones in preparation for integration numbered as high as Ship 51. SpaceX officials stated that the company is currently completing one Ship upper stage every two weeks and one Super Heavy booster every four weeks, with overlapping production allowing multiple rockets to move through the factory simultaneously. The majority of vehicles currently being assembled are intended to carry stacks of SpaceX’s upgraded Starlink Version 3 (V3) satellites.

The manufacturing process is modeled after the automotive industry, prioritizing efficiency and the reproduction of identical parts. While automation is a critical component, SpaceX engineers have designed much of the equipment and deliberately kept technicians on the floor to refine production processes and eliminate bottlenecks. A tour guide compared the company’s manufacturing consistency goals to the precision of Lego bricks. Outside the main building, the facility includes two Mega Bays for stacking and integrating Starship sections with their engines, each holding about five or six assemblies. Adjacent to these is the Gigabay, currently under construction, which will cover approximately 700,000 square feet and accommodate up to 24 vehicles at a time.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has stated that the company hopes to launch Starship about once a week beginning in 2027. The Starlink network in low Earth orbit currently consists of more than 11,000 spacecraft, most of which were launched on Falcon 9 rockets, with a few more than 50 delivered on Starship’s two most recent test flights. SpaceX officials noted that each of these recent Starship launches added data capacity equivalent to ten Falcon 9 Starlink launches. The company aims to increase launch cadence dramatically to grow the Starlink network, with the inventory of Ships seen in Starfactory suggesting that launch vehicle supply will not be a limiting factor for this goal.

Later that day, the Super Heavy booster attempted a return to the pad but was diverted for an offshore landing, where it exploded. The following day, Ship 42 returned to the launch site, lit its engines, and was caught by the launch tower. This sequence of events occurred during the same weekend as the media tour, highlighting the operational milestones achieved by the Starship program.
summary: SpaceX invited media to tour its Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, where it manufactures Starship rockets using an automotive-style production process. The facility is currently producing one upper stage every two weeks and one booster every four weeks to support Starlink satellite launches and the Artemis program.
author: Space.com

title: Andrey Zvyagintsev on 40-day coma, 92% lung damage, and life in exile
content: The Russian film-maker spent 40 days in a coma and suffered 92% lung damage during the pandemic. He describes how making new movie Minotaur helped his rehabilitation Andrey Zvyagintsev tells the tale of a knight who is riding through a dark forest and sees a stone sign at a fork in the road. The sign says that if he turns left he will lose his horse and if he turns right he will lose his head. So the knight has a dilemma; there are only bad options here. Zvyagintsev smiles and says: “It is a very Russian fairytale.” Terrible things tend to happen, that’s the way the world works, and a person is defined by how they respond to each challenge. That goes for the knight in the forest and the characters in a film. It probably goes for Zvyagintsev, too, who has lost not his horse but his home and very nearly his life. The Russian director almost died during the Covid-19 pandemic and spent 40 days in an induced coma. He now lives in exile as an enemy of the state. “I’m with the birds,” he says by way of explaining his situation. “Birds have no borders. They’re not thinking about tomorrow.”
summary: Russian film-maker Andrey Zvyagintsev spent 40 days in a coma and suffered 92% lung damage during the pandemic. He now lives in exile as an enemy of the state and describes how making his new movie Minotaur helped his rehabilitation.
author: Guardian Culture

title: HBO drama War features Dominic West and Sienna Miller in tech scandal plot
content:
The HBO/Sky legal thriller War is approaching its explosive finale, with critics noting that the on-screen divorce battle between Dominic West and Sienna Miller offers a compelling drama. The narrative centers on Morgan Henderson, a billionaire social media mogul played by West, who engages in a hotel affair with an unknown woman following an awards show. This individual is revealed to be collaborating with Henderson’s wife, Hollywood star Carla Duval, portrayed by Miller, to expose his infidelity.

The article draws a parallel between the show’s plot and recent real-world events involving Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang. According to the text, Huang resigned after revelations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a situation described as a honeytrap that brought down a tech titan. The piece suggests that this real-life scandal makes the fictional legal thriller feel particularly timely as it nears its conclusion.
summary: The legal thriller War stars Dominic West as a tech titan caught in a honeytrap orchestrated by his wife, played by Sienna Miller. The show's plot mirrors the recent resignation of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang following revelations of an affair with a suspected spy.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Steps Review: Netflix's Cinderella Rework Has Pep Despite Overstuffed Plot
content: The plot might be a little overstuffed and the animation style could be a little more distinctive, but this is better than the streamer’s average animated offering Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but that age-old story you think you know, well, you might not know it at all. It’s a tale as old as Shrek, which was by no means the first film to subvert fairytale expectations, but it was definitely the most influential, and we’re still feeling its impact 25 years later, for better or worse. What if that villain wasn’t actually the villain after all? What if that love interest shouldn’t have been of interest in the first place? What if that damsel in distress was given a bullet-speed fight scene instead of weeping in a tower? But what might have seemed fresh in 2001, if not quite as fresh for anyone who knew and loved The Princess Bride, has grown a little tiresome ever since. Bucking the conventions has essentially become the convention, and effortful attempts to remix classic storytelling beats have mostly ended up reeking of smugness. Yet they still keep coming (IP is king) and before the inevitable Shrek legacy sequel hits cinemas next summer, Netflix is trying to conjure up that same mix of snark and sentiment with Steps, a Cinderella story but, wait for it, not the Cinderella story you thought you knew …
summary: The review states that while Steps has an overstuffed plot and lacks a distinctive animation style, it is better than Netflix's average animated offering. The film is described as a Cinderella rework that attempts to mix snark and sentiment in a subverted fairytale story.
author: Guardian Culture

title: New David O. Russell biopic shows John Madden animated during horse stunt
content:
A new biopic directed by David O. Russell has just been released, chronicling the career of the coach‑turned‑commentator‑turned‑gaming icon John Madden. Those familiar with Madden’s life recall his singular career in the NFL, notably his time with the Oakland Raiders.  

During a training session, former player Ted Hendricks, wearing an Oakland Raiders uniform and helmet, entered the field on a roan horse while holding an orange traffic cone like a lance. He stopped at the 50‑yard line, an act that could have provoked anger from some coaches. Madden, however, remained unfazed. Hendricks, now 79, said the stunt was a spur‑of‑the‑moment idea that “put a smile on everyone’s face.” After Hendricks dismounted, Madden called the team together, saying, “All right guys, Ted’s here, let’s get started.” Madden later remarked on the look on Hendricks’ face and the comments he made in interviews, indicating he too enjoyed the moment.
summary: New David O. Russell biopic shows John Madden animated during horse stunt.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Yankees Sign Jonathan Loáisiga to Two-Year Deal
content: The New York Yankees have reached an agreement with right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga on a two-year contract that includes a club option for 2029, according to sources told ESPN. This deal reunites the reliever with the club following a season apart.
summary: The Yankees and right‑hander Jonathan Loáisiga have agreed to a two‑year contract with a club option for 2029, according to sources told ESPN. The deal reunites the reliever with the club after a season apart.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Arsenal's Lisa Baum: 'I believe in us. I think it's all about the small margins'
content: Germany forward on her new life in London and drawing strength from the memory of her late brother, Dennis Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining. Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.
summary: Germany forward Lisa Baum scored the winning goal in her Arsenal debut against Brighton in Crawley. The 19-year-old winger joined the club less than two months before her first appearance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: ATP boosts men's tennis prize money to over $350m by 2028
content: Cash increase via ATP’s creation of ‘One Vision’ company More rest breaks added to reduce player welfare issues The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year. The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.
summary: The ATP has approved a financial overhaul that will increase total player prize money from $270m to more than $350m by 2028. This increase is funded by the creation of ATP Ventures, which will sell the tour's media, commercial, and data rights.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mitch Marsh skips press conference as Australia T20 series begins at MCG
content:
Mitch Marsh, Australia’s white-ball captain, is not expected to attend press conferences ahead of the Twenty20 series against England, which begins Saturday at the MCG. This decision follows a contentious press conference held before the recent one-day series, where a febrile atmosphere reportedly developed. In Marsh’s absence, Victoria’s Sam Harper addressed the media to discuss his upcoming debut at the MCG.

The 29-year-old wicketkeeper, who has previously overcome troubling concussions, provided a local angle for the coverage. However, his appearance was viewed as a somewhat optimistic attempt to shift focus away from the ongoing sandpaper controversy in Australia.
summary: Australia white-ball captain Mitch Marsh is not expected at press conferences amid a febrile atmosphere in Australia. Sam Harper spoke at the event instead, providing a local angle ahead of the Twenty20s starting at the MCG.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wales make four changes to beat Australia after All Blacks win
content:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy has announced four changes to the squad for Saturday night’s match against Australia in Cardiff. The selection follows Wales’ historic victory over the All Blacks, marking the first win against the New Zealand side in 73 years. Despite the magnitude of that achievement, the coaching team opted for significant rotation rather than maintaining the previous lineup, a decision described as an approach to adding both depth and quality to the current generation of players.

The roster adjustments include the absence of Adam Beard due to a shoulder injury, which is expected to keep him out until the finals next weekend. Additionally, three other players have been dropped or rested, a group that includes the player named as the match winner in the previous game against the All Blacks. The coaching staff views these changes as a way to strengthen the team as it continues to support the structures of Welsh rugby.
summary: Steve Tandy has made four changes to the Wales team to face Australia in Cardiff following their first victory over New Zealand in 73 years. The squad adjustments include resting players and addressing Adam Beard's shoulder injury while maintaining team depth and quality.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Liverpool fan found not guilty of abusing Semenyo
content:
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution, according to the Press Association. The trial of Mark Mogan, 47, took place at Liverpool Magistrates’ Court, where Semenyo was originally scheduled to provide evidence on Friday.

The accusation stemmed from an incident during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club, Bournemouth, at Anfield on August 15 last year. Mogan had been charged with shouting abuse during that fixture.
summary: A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo was found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution. The trial at Liverpool Magistrates' Court involved Mark Mogan, who was accused of shouting abuse during a Premier League match at Anfield.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Stafford McDowall named Scotland captain after Rory Darge injury
content: Stafford McDowall, who was working on his father’s farm, received a call to play for Scotland against Australia on Sunday. Six days later, he will serve as captain for the match against Japan following a late injury to Rory Darge.
summary: Stafford McDowall was called to play for Scotland against Australia while working on his dad's farm. He will serve as captain against Japan six days later after Rory Darge suffered a late injury blow.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua suspended three games after assault lawsuit
content: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua received a three‑game suspension for violating the NFL’s personal‑conduct policy, a penalty that followed an assault lawsuit. The suspension was imposed while Nacua was already sidelined with an injury.
summary: Puka Nacua was given a three-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy. He was already out injured at the time of the suspension.
author: BBC Sport

title: Don Lemon says he will run for president if Democrats reverse dark money ruling
content: Independent journalist Don Lemon stated he would run for president if Democrats could reverse the Supreme Court decision that allowed dark money into politics. Lemon told podcast host David Sirota that he would “100 percent” launch a bid for the White House under those specific conditions.
summary: Don Lemon stated he would launch a presidential bid if Democrats could reverse the Supreme Court decision that allowed dark money into politics. Lemon told podcast host David Sirota that he would "100 percent" run for the White House under those conditions.
author: The Hill

title: Poland says Russian missiles and drone violated airspace
content: Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz stated on Friday that Russian objects violated Polish airspace overnight. The minister confirmed an incursion involving two missiles and a drone from the Russian Federation, according to a Reuters report.
summary: Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz stated that two missiles and a drone from the Russian Federation violated Polish airspace overnight. The minister confirmed the incursion during a press conference reported by Reuters.
author: The Hill

title: DOJ clears NextEra-Dominion merger despite electricity cost concerns
content: The Department of Justice approved the merger between energy companies NextEra and Dominion on Thursday. The agency’s release noted concerns regarding the deal’s potential impact on electricity costs. Additionally, the DOJ stated that the Internal Market Monitor of ISO New England, which oversees the region’s electric power system, submitted comments on the transaction.
summary: The Department of Justice approved the merger between energy companies NextEra and Dominion on Thursday. The agency noted concerns about the deal's potential impact on electricity costs while acknowledging comments from the ISO New England Internal Market Monitor.
author: The Hill

title: Zinke says Republicans moving on from Trump after midterm losses
content: GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke (Mont.) on Thursday evening indicated that Republican lawmakers are distancing themselves from President Trump after they lost control of Congress in the midterm elections. “They’re moving on, but no doubt, the president took a little pain off them,” Zinke told host Blake Burman on NewsNation’s “The Hill.” “And I would say,…
summary: GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke stated that Republican lawmakers are distancing themselves from President Trump following their loss of control of Congress. Zinke noted that the president took some political pain off the party members during the midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Speaker Mike Johnson urges House Republicans to show up and vote
content: Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) urged House Republicans to remain fully engaged and show up for work in a letter posted to X on Friday. This call to action followed the postponement of a procedural rule vote earlier in the week due to member absences. Johnson emphasized the need for every Republican to stay involved over the next 44 days.
summary: Speaker Mike Johnson urged House Republicans to remain fully engaged over the next 44 days. He made this request after GOP leaders postponed a procedural rule vote earlier this week due to member absences.
author: The Hill

title: U.S. economic performance varies by data source and individual perspective
content: The U.S. economy's condition varies depending on the data source and the perspective of the individual being asked.
summary: U.S. economic performance varies by data source and individual perspective.
author: The Hill

title: New York City unveils plan to close Rikers Island jail complex
content: New York City officials are advancing plans to close Rikers, the city’s main jail complex, after years of discussion. The facility has faced ongoing issues, including assaults and inmate deaths.
summary: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex. The facility has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.
author: NPR Politics

title: Senate passes bipartisan bill to speed data center and power plant approvals
content: The Senate passed a bipartisan energy bill designed to expedite the approval process for data centers and power plants. This legislative action comes as Americans face rising energy costs and heightened demand driven by artificial intelligence, though the bill has also drawn environmental concerns.
summary: The Senate passed a bipartisan bill designed to accelerate the approval process for data centers and power plants. This action comes amid rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI.
author: NPR Politics

title: Dems seek to block Iran war funding; Army delays lead azide detonation
content: Democrats are positioning to block Iran war funding as Congress works to pass a measure to prevent a government shutdown next month. Additionally, the Army has delayed the detonation of lead azide in Iowa, citing concerns that further waiting could pose safety risks.
summary: Democrats aim to use the upcoming funding measure to block Iran war funding before a government shutdown. The Army stated that waiting to detonate lead azide in Iowa could become dangerous.
author: NPR Politics

title: Texas execution over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Dennes moaned about pain
content: On the day Reinaldo Dennes received lethal injection in Texas, the execution lasted over an hour as staff struggled to locate a vein, and Dennes moaned about pain. Meanwhile, Florida carried out its record‑breaking 20th execution of the year.
summary: The Texas execution of Reinaldo Dennes lasted over an hour as staff struggled to locate a vein and he moaned about pain. On the same day, Florida carried out its record‑breaking 20th execution of the year.
author: NPR Politics

title: Trump to hold press conference after meetings with Xi and Putin
content: Trump is set to hold a press conference after meeting with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin. During his recent trip to China, he did not formally take questions at the end of the visit, although such a session is typically expected on presidential foreign trips.
summary: Trump will hold a press conference after his meetings with Xi and Putin. He did not formally take questions while in China at the end of his trip.
author: NPR Politics

title: Brussels summit could shape UK-EU deal on food, energy, and youth mobility
content: BBC political editor Chris Mason examines the potential outcomes of the Brussels summit regarding the UK-EU Brexit deal. The analysis focuses on possible agreements between the two parties concerning food, energy, and youth mobility.
summary: BBC political editor Chris Mason examines potential agreements between the UK and the EU. The discussion focuses on possible outcomes regarding food, energy, and youth mobility.
author: BBC Politics

title: War in Iran turns Strait of Hormuz into climate catastrophe with oil spills
content:
The war between the US, Israel, and Iran has transformed the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil shipping route, into a battlefield and the epicenter of a growing environmental crisis. According to a video explainer by The Guardian, tankers hit by missiles or sea mines are leaking oil into the Gulf. This has resulted in extensive oil slicks that are visible from space, staining coastlines and posing a threat of lasting harm to marine ecosystems.

Because the area remains inaccessible due to a naval blockade, documenting the full extent of the damage on the ground is nearly impossible. To assess the scale of the devastation, The Guardian analyzed dozens of satellite images and consulted with environmental experts. The investigation highlights the severe impact of these boat strikes on the fragile ecosystems of the Gulf, emphasizing the difficulty of evaluating the environmental consequences from a distance.
summary: Tankers struck by missiles or sea mines are leaking oil into the Gulf, creating vast slicks that threaten marine ecosystems. The Guardian examined satellite images and spoke to experts to assess the damage, noting that naval blockades prevent on-ground documentation.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Cop31 talks enter overtime without new draft deal as activists call summit worst ever
content: Fossil fuels and climate finance among deep divisions that have pushed UN summit beyond its official end Antalya 2026 is the “worst Cop ever”, civil society activists have said in a packed final press conference at the UN climate summit. Civil society organisations have a special status at UN climate treaty summits. They have the right to observe and even intervene in negotiations, although decisions are ultimately taken by the countries that are parties to the UNFCCC.
summary: UN climate talks in Antalya have extended beyond their official end due to deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Civil society activists described the event as the worst Cop ever during a final press conference.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US fishers view offshore wind as 'godsend' despite Trump's opposition
content: Despite the president’s attacks, Sea Services is training New England fishers in offshore wind construction and providing them with a second income stream On a rainy September morning, the Pamela Ann, a rusty, 86ft (26-metre) scallop boat, docked in New Bedford, Massachusetts. Its crew had spent the past 12 days at sea, recording mammal sightings, monitoring vessels to ensure they didn’t enter construction zones, and keeping watch over workers at Revolution Wind, a 65-turbine offshore wind project just south of Rhode Island. “God forbid, if anybody was to fall, we could be there to help them out,” said Capt Kevin Souza, who has a bulldog tattoo on his shin to mark his time in the navy.
summary: Sea Services is training New England fishers in offshore wind construction to provide them with a second income stream. Capt Kevin Souza's crew monitors vessels and workers at the Revolution Wind project to ensure safety and compliance.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews for energy projects and datacenters
content:
The U.S. Senate approved bipartisan legislation on Thursday that will move to the House. The bill is designed to speed up permitting reviews for power plants, transmission lines, and other energy infrastructure, with the aim of increasing the nation’s energy supplies to meet surging demand and lower electricity prices.

The legislation would shorten the timeline for starting large energy projects and requires datacenters to pay for the energy they use. Some Democrats and environmental groups have expressed concerns, citing anger over datacenters and rising electricity prices that has prompted a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on energy‑hungry behemoths.
summary: US Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews for energy projects and datacenters.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Lund University finds galectin-3 drives microglia response and plaque formation in Alzheimer's
content: Researchers at Lund University in Sweden have found that the protein galectin‑3 plays a key role in Alzheimer’s disease. The study shows that galectin‑3 influences how microglia, the brain’s immune cells, respond to amyloid plaques, and it also shapes the plaques themselves. Additionally, galectin‑3 may contribute to the nerve damage that develops around these plaques.
summary: Researchers at Lund University identified a key role for galectin-3 in Alzheimer's disease. The protein influences microglia reactions to amyloid plaques and may contribute to nerve damage around the plaques.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Researchers create NeuroAxis implant that uses glucose fuel cell to monitor diabetes
content: Researchers have created an experimental implant named NeuroAxis that employs a glucose fuel cell to harvest energy from high blood sugar levels. The device also senses metabolic fluctuations in real time, offering a new approach to monitoring and potentially improving glucose control in type 2 diabetes.
summary: High blood sugar, a major problem in type 2 diabetes, could become part of the solution in monitoring the disease. Researchers have developed an experimental implant called NeuroAxis that uses a glucose fuel cell to harvest energy and sense metabolic fluctuations in real time.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experimental MYC inhibitor drug directly targets lung cancer cells and aids immune attack
content: Researchers have discovered that an experimental MYC inhibitor drug attacks lung cancer cells directly while also increasing their visibility to the immune system. In a series of experiments, the drug was shown to make cancer cells easier for immune cells to target and kill.
summary: Researchers found that an experimental MYC inhibitor drug directly targets lung cancer cells. The drug also makes the cancer cells easier for the immune system to target and kill.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Liver Model Developed to Study Alpha‑1‑Antitrypsin Deficiency
content:
A new liver model has been developed to study alpha‑1‑antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), a rare genetic metabolic disorder that affects the liver and lungs.

The mutation causes hepatocytes to produce misfolded alpha‑1‑antitrypsin, reducing its secretion into blood plasma. AAT normally mitigates inflammatory reactions that can lead to tissue damage.
summary: A new liver model has been developed to study alpha‑1‑antitrypsin deficiency, a rare genetic metabolic disorder that affects the liver and lungs. The model allows investigation of how a mutation causes hepatocytes to produce misfolded alpha‑1‑antitrypsin, leading to reduced secretion into blood plasma and impaired control of inflammatory processes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Late-night phone use linked to shorter sleep in teens, especially girls
content:
Late‑night phone use is increasingly common among teens, who often check the first notification after turning off their alarm and then scroll through reels until they feel sleepy. For many, a phone is always within reach.

Excessive screen time has been linked to physical and mental health problems in adolescents. The impact is especially pronounced for those who are vulnerable to body‑image concerns, a group that may experience deeper effects from prolonged device use.

Scientists suspect that the negative consequences of late‑night scrolling extend beyond the waking hours, potentially shortening sleep duration and disrupting the body’s essential daily routine.
summary: Late-night phone use has been linked to shorter sleep among teenagers, especially girls. Scientists suspect that excessive screen time can extend its effects beyond waking hours into sleep, adding to the physical and mental health problems already associated with teen screen use.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Living in a disadvantaged neighborhood associated with socioemotional, behavioral concerns in young children
content:
Neighborhoods that have historically been deprived of resources exhibit clear disparities compared with better‑resourced areas. These disparities include lower school quality, fewer green spaces, and poorer physical and mental health outcomes for residents.  

Prior studies of neighborhood deprivation have typically examined only one or two indicators in isolation—such as children’s opportunities or the risk of illness during extreme heat. Those investigations have also focused on adults or school‑age children, rather than on younger children’s broader socioemotional and behavioral development.
summary: Living in a disadvantaged neighborhood associated with socioemotional, behavioral concerns in young children.
author: Medical Xpress

title: PTSD May Shape Brain Differently by Gender, Race, and Trauma Age
content: Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). A study published in the journal Cell Reports on Nov. 20 that examined the postmortem brains of 101 people with PTSD found that genes associated with PTSD varied more than expected across different brain regions when it comes to DNA methylation, a natural biological process that acts like a genetic "dimmer switch" for genes, sometimes blocking genetic code entirely.
summary: A study published in Cell Reports on Nov. 20 examined postmortem brains of 101 people with PTSD. The study found that genes linked to PTSD varied more than expected across different brain regions in DNA methylation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: National survey finds clinicians often fail to document recognized opioid misuse
content: A national survey of 1,470 primary‑care clinicians, conducted by researchers at Wake Forest University School of Medicine, found that when clinicians recognized opioid misuse in their patients, they did not always document the issue in the medical record.
summary: Primary care clinicians who recognized opioid misuse in their patients did not always record it in the medical record. The finding comes from a national survey of 1,470 clinicians conducted by researchers at Wake Forest University School of Medicine.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Former GM CEO Dan Akerson says new GM will face tough succession amid tech shift
content: Former GM CEO Dan Akerson stated that the successor to Mary Barra will face a challenging role. He explained that the incoming leader will inherit a period of rapid change within both the technology sector and the broader auto industry.
summary: Former GM CEO Dan Akerson says whoever replaces Mary Barra will face a difficult task. The difficulty stems from inheriting rapid change in technology and the auto industry.
author: CNBC Business

title: UK and EU to Hold Second Brexit Summit in Brussels Amid Economic Volatility
content:
The UK and EU are set to hold their second summit since Brexit in Brussels on Friday, a meeting taking place against a volatile economic backdrop. The summit coincides with the war in the Middle East impacting the global economy.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham will attend the event to meet with Ursula von der Leyen, head of the European Commission, and António Costa, president of the European Council. The gathering is part of ongoing discussions in Brussels regarding closer relations between the two entities.
summary: The UK and EU will hold their second summit since Brexit in Brussels on Friday amid a volatile economic backdrop. The meeting will involve UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, EU Commission head Ursula von der Leyen, and European Council president António Costa.
author: Guardian Business

title: California subpoenas Nvidia over chip export scandal after Jensen Huang leaves
content:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia following a scandal that led to the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang. The subpoena is part of an inquiry into whether exports of the company’s advanced semiconductor chips reached China in violation of US restrictions.

Bonta stated that the conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises "bright red flags," including potential misleading of investors. He emphasized that while Nvidia faces a complex transnational situation, corporate securities law clearly prohibits companies from misleading their investors.
summary: California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co‑founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang. Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena to investigate whether Nvidia’s advanced semiconductor chips were exported to China, potentially violating US restrictions.
author: Guardian Business

title: Botanist A. H. S. Lucas discovers new seaweed species near Lord Howe Island
content: Botanist A. H. S. Lucas identified and named the seaweed Sargassum howeanum in 1935 after collecting large adult specimens near Lord Howe Island. The World Heritage–listed site is recognized for its unique biodiversity, and the newly found tangle of long, caramel-colored seaweed had not been spotted in 90 years.
summary: A tangle of long, caramel-colored seaweed. That's what botanist A.
