title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet in Shenzhen on Ukraine and Nuclear Issues
content: President Trump, China’s Xi Jinping, and Russia’s Vladimir Putin convened for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. The agenda for the historic gathering included discussions on Ukraine, Iran, and nuclear disarmament.
summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russia's Vladimir Putin gathered in Shenzhen, China, for a historic trilateral meeting. The agenda for the meeting included discussions on Ukraine, Iran, and nuclear disarmament.
author: NPR Politics

title: US sells first deep-sea mining leases near American Samoa despite court ruling
content: Multi-million dollar sale comes despite a federal judge in Hawaii voiding the environmental clearance it had been given to proceed The US has carried out its first ever deep-sea mining lease sales off the coast of American Samoa, despite an adverse court ruling earlier this week and mounting local opposition. The sales took place on Thursday in a live-streamed auction of 12.7m hectares (31.5m acres) of seabed off the US territory’s coast marked for mineral exploration. Two areas of the Pacific archipelago were sold for $3m each to Wetstone US Ventures, the only bidder, according to a spokesperson for the Marine Minerals Administration (MMA).
summary: The US conducted its first deep-sea mining lease sale off American Samoa, auctioning 12.7 million hectares of seabed to Wetstone US Ventures. The sale proceeded for $3 million per area despite a federal judge in Hawaii voiding the environmental clearance and local opposition.
author: Guardian Environment

title: ChatGPT translation of mental health questionnaires into Mandarin inconsistent
content: As Asian New Zealanders increasingly report mental health challenges, a researcher at Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury is investigating whether artificial intelligence can bridge language barriers when human translation resources are limited. The study examines ChatGPT’s translation of mental health questionnaires into Mandarin, noting that the results were inconsistent.
summary: ChatGPT's translation of mental health questionnaires into Mandarin produced inconsistent results. A Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) researcher is asking whether AI can bridge language barriers as more Asian New Zealanders report mental health challenges.
author: Medical Xpress

title: State-by-state scorecard reveals wide gaps in access to obesity treatments
content: A new state-by-state scorecard and report reveals significant disparities in Americans' access to obesity treatment based on their location. The analysis assigns D or F grades to 20 states and identifies substantial barriers to care in every state across the nation, highlighting wide gaps in healthcare availability.
summary: A new state-by-state scorecard and report finds significant barriers to obesity care in every state in the nation. The report assigns D or F grades to 20 states, highlighting how location affects treatment access.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Australian startup Lubdub begins clinical trial of waterproof wearable heart monitor
content:
A lightweight, gel‑free, waterproof heart monitor is now being tested in an Australian clinic. The device offers real‑time insights into heart health while users go about their daily activities.

The patch was originally invented through research at RMIT University and is now being developed by the Australian startup Lubdub. It is a wireless patch that continuously tracks the heart’s rhythm for up to 14 days.

During the clinical trial, doctors will receive the same detailed information from the patch as they would from a medical‑grade electrocardiogram (ECG) Holter monitor.
summary: The lightweight, gel‑free, waterproof wearable patch that tracks heart rhythm for up to 14 days is being trialed at an Australian clinic. It was invented through research at RMIT University and is now being developed by Australian startup Lubdub, providing real‑time data comparable to a medical‑grade ECG Holter monitor.
author: Medical Xpress

title: At least 178 pregnant Americans infected with measles since 2025
content: At least 178 pregnant Americans have contracted measles since 2025. The virus poses significant risks to expectant mothers and their babies, making recovery from such an infection a notable outcome for affected individuals.
summary: At least 178 pregnant Americans have been infected with measles since 2025. The measles virus poses dangers to expectant mothers and babies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Pennsylvania logs measles death as survey finds confusion over risks
content: Pennsylvania has recorded another measles death, according to a report released by the Annenberg Public Policy Center at the University of Pennsylvania. The same release includes a survey of over 1,000 adults indicating that many Americans are confused about measles risks and the safety and benefits of childhood vaccines.
summary: A survey of more than 1,000 adults by the Annenberg Public Policy Center found that many Americans are confused about the risks of measles and the safety of childhood vaccines. This finding was released as Pennsylvania logged another measles death.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Paramedics need time and support to recover between emergency calls
content: Paramedics often transition directly from one emergency response to another, leaving minimal time to process the previous incident before the next call arrives. This continuous cycle highlights the need for adequate time and support to allow professionals to recover between urgent duties.
summary: Paramedics often move directly from one emergency call to the next with little time to process the previous incident. This lack of recovery time highlights the need for support to help them manage the emotional demands of their work.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Half of NHS trusts breach guidelines by treating vulnerable patients in corridors
content: Exclusive data published in The BMJ indicate that half of hospital trusts in England are violating NHS corridor care guidelines. These breaches involve treating vulnerable patients, including children, mental health patients, and individuals with physical or learning disabilities, in emergency department corridors.
summary: Data published by The BMJ reveal that half of hospital trusts in England are breaching NHS corridor care guidelines. These trusts are treating vulnerable groups, including children and those with disabilities, in emergency department corridors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Singapore reports 65% decline in cervical cancer mortality since 1990
content:
Cervical cancer mortality in Singapore has declined by 65% since 1990, though screening gaps persist. The condition remains one of the few cancers potentially eliminable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, regular screening, and timely treatment of precancerous changes. Despite these effective prevention and treatment measures, global cervical cancer deaths are projected to increase by nearly 40% by 2050.

These findings come from a study involving researchers from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (NUS Medicine), and the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington. The research highlights the contrast between Singapore’s significant progress and the anticipated rise in global mortality rates.
summary: Singapore has seen a 65% decline in cervical cancer mortality since 1990, yet screening gaps remain. A study by researchers from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS Medicine, and the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation projected that global cervical cancer deaths will rise by nearly 40% by 2050.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Ophiopogon longiscapus Species Discovered in Yunnan Wenshan Reserve
content: Botanists have described a new mondo grass species, Ophiopogon longiscapus, from the Yunnan Wenshan National Nature Reserve in southeastern China. The plant is named for its unusually long flowering stalk, or scape.
summary: Botanists described a new Ophiopogon species in the Yunnan Wenshan National Nature Reserve, southeastern China. The species, named Ophiopogon longiscapus, was named for its unusually long flowering stalk, or scape.
author: Phys.org

title: Innovative technology offers a bold new vision for monitoring ocean health
content: MBARI's research vessel Paragon departed from Moss Landing early in October, carrying three robots on its deck. The launch occurred as Monterey Bay showcased its marine environment, underscoring the use of innovative technology for monitoring ocean health.
summary: Innovative technology offers a bold new vision for monitoring ocean health.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers Build Structured-Light Systems in Three Dimensions
content:
Structured‑light technology has emerged as a vital tool in modern optics, enabling researchers to shape light fields by controlling amplitude, phase, polarization, and spatial mode. These engineered fields extend beyond the capabilities of conventional laser beams and are being applied in communications, imaging, sensing, optical computing, and quantum photonics.

Despite these advances, many structured‑light systems still depend on multiple discrete optical components. The components require careful alignment and occupy significant space, limiting compactness and ease of use in practical applications.
summary: Structured light allows shaping amplitude, phase, polarization and spatial mode to create light fields beyond conventional laser beams. Many current structured-light systems still rely on multiple discrete optical components that require careful alignment and occupy significant space.
author: Phys.org

title: AI virtual cell technology may reveal how genetic changes and drugs alter cells
content: Artificial intelligence models today can predict whether a person carrying a genetic change will develop a disease. However, they fall short of answering two critical questions: why the disease occurs and how to design an effective treatment. AI virtual‑cell technology is being explored as a way to reveal how genetic alterations and drugs alter cellular behavior.
summary: Current artificial intelligence models can predict whether a person with a genetic change will develop a disease. However, they cannot explain why the disease occurs or how to design a treatment.
author: Phys.org

title: IEA report says extreme weather raises risks to global oil and gas shipping
content: The International Energy Agency reports that extreme weather events are increasingly threatening international oil and natural gas shipping. According to the new IEA report, such events could damage critical infrastructure, disrupt major trade routes and jeopardize energy security.
summary: A new IEA report says extreme weather events are creating significant risks for international oil and natural gas shipping. The report warns that such events could damage critical infrastructure, disrupt major trade routes and threaten energy security.
author: Phys.org

title: UCT research: Nature-based solutions must shift to power-sharing in informal settlements
content:
New research from UCT finds that nature‑based solutions for climate adaptation are failing informal settlements.  
The study argues that solutions must shift from mere participation to power‑sharing partnerships that acknowledge residents’ lived experiences and their relationships with nature.
summary: New research from UCT indicates that nature-based solutions for climate adaptation are failing informal settlements. The study argues these solutions must move beyond participation to power-sharing partnerships that recognize lived experiences and relationships with nature.
author: Phys.org

title: MIT study finds data centers harm air quality far from their locations
content: A new study by MIT researchers indicates that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence data centers causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from the physical facilities.
summary: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick‑and‑mortar facilities are located. The findings are reported in a new study by MIT researchers.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists link CDK12 gene mutation to aggressive prostate cancer
content: Scientists discovered a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene linked to aggressive prostate cancer. All five identified carriers developed metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. The finding could lead to expanded genetic testing, helping families uncover hidden cancer risks and potentially detect the disease while it is still treatable.
summary: Researchers identified a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene associated with aggressive prostate cancer, noting that all five carriers developed metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. This discovery may enable expanded genetic testing to help families uncover hidden cancer risks and detect the disease while it is still treatable.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Narrow Search for Stonehenge's Six-Ton Altar Stone, Point to Scotland
content:
A new investigation into Stonehenge’s six‑ton Altar Stone has yielded fresh clues while eliminating several earlier theories. Researchers have ruled out a Welsh origin and now consider the massive sandstone slab to have come from northeastern Scotland.

Despite this narrowed focus, scientists have yet to locate an exact source match for the stone, leaving the mystery of its provenance unresolved.
summary: Researchers have ruled out several suspected sources for Stonehenge’s six‑ton Altar Stone. The slab, once thought to be from Wales, is now believed to have come from northeastern Scotland, though no exact match has been found.
author: Science Daily

title: Excessive Exercise May Leave Brain in Overdrive
content:
Scientists discovered that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training without adequate recovery exhibited elevated dopamine levels in a brain region associated with memory and emotions. These elevated levels persisted for at least 48 hours after the exercise sessions ended.

This finding offers a potential explanation for why overtrained athletes may experience symptoms such as insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although the study did not directly measure these specific conditions in the animals.
summary: Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising. The discovery could help explain why overtrained athletes sometimes struggle with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although these symptoms were not directly measured.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds Antarctica's ice cliffs stabilize rather than collapse catastrophically
content: A new study indicates that Antarctica’s towering ice cliffs may be less prone to catastrophic collapse than previously thought. By tracking over 15,000 ice cliffs, researchers found that even the tallest formations, which can collapse at alarming speeds, often stabilize rather than triggering an unstoppable chain reaction. The study suggests that underwater ridges, surrounding water, and broken ice provide natural defenses against further collapse.
summary: A new study tracking more than 15,000 ice cliffs suggests they are less vulnerable to catastrophic collapse than previously feared. Researchers found that underwater ridges, surrounding water, and broken ice help stabilize the tallest cliffs.
author: Science Daily

title: BepiColombo Arrives at Mercury, Prepares for Second‑Ever Orbit
content:
The BepiColombo double probe has arrived at Mercury after a journey exceeding eight years and 6 billion miles. This joint European-Japanese mission is set to become the second in history to enter orbit around the smallest planet in the solar system. Flight controllers are scheduled to fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday to initiate the orbital insertion.

Once in orbit, the mission will map Mercury’s surface and study its interior. These activities aim to provide insights into the planet’s unusually large core, contributing to the exploration of this barely explored world.
summary: BepiColombo Arrives at Mercury, Prepares for Second‑Ever Orbit.
author: Guardian Science

title: Cyclone Xavier Becomes Record-Setting Category 5 Storm in Southwest Pacific
content:
On November 15, 2026, the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates regarding a slow-moving tropical disturbance located northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within days, this system intensified rapidly into one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier, the storm developed in an environment characterized by minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit), conditions well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones. Xavier was the second named storm of the 2026 season, following a short-lived October storm named Wati.

NASA satellite data indicated that Xavier churned along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water stretching from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific, a sign of the El Niño present in the region since June. When the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured an image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026, forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Later that day, winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour, classifying the storm as a Category 5 on the regional cyclone intensity scale or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale. Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach noted that Xavier ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record.

The storm’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual but aligns with research indicating that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Studies also suggest that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace. According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. The system subsequently encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment, causing it to weaken as it pushed westward and reducing the threat to Samoa and American Samoa.

Looking ahead, the Fiji Meteorological Service projects that the region could see between 11 and 15 named tropical cyclones this season, with the greatest risk located east of the international date line. Storm activity in the Southwest Pacific basin typically peaks in February, suggesting Xavier may be one of several storms to affect the area in the coming months. The image accompanying this report was taken by Lauren Dauphin using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview, with the story written by Adam Voiland.
summary: Cyclone Xavier intensified rapidly in the Southwest Pacific, reaching peak winds of 220 km/h (140 mph) and becoming the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record. The storm damaged homes and caused power disruptions in the northern Cook Islands before weakening and reducing the threat to Samoa and American Samoa.
author: NASA News

title: Voyager 1 receives Morse code message from Earth, one light-day away
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity’s most distant interstellar spacecraft? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day. In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. For extra credit, fans of math can calculate that at one light-day per 50 years, Voyager 1 will reach its one light-year (365 light-days) distance milestone in about 18,250 years. Tomorrow’s picture: pixels in space Date: November 20, 2026 Credit & Copyright: Apostolos Kyriazis Authors & editors: Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. U. Random APOD Generator Yesterday’s Image APOD: 2026 November 19 – The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas Tomorrow’s Image
summary: On November 17, fans used a flashlight beam at the Emirates Astronomical Observatory to send a Morse code message to Voyager 1, which was captured in a time exposure. The message traveled at the speed of light and reached Voyager 1 one day later, on November 18 at 10:16:07 UTC, marking its one light-day milestone.
author: NASA News

title: Gig Work Invades Nursing Homes, Leading to Dangerous Mistakes
content: A WIRED and Proof News investigation has found that inspection reports of elder‑care facilities reveal a serious problem: when new workers receive little or no onboarding, dangerous mistakes can occur and nurses become overwhelmed. The reports highlight the risks of gig work in nursing homes.
summary: Inspection reports reveal that elder care facilities often lack proper worker onboarding. This can cause dangerous mistakes and overwhelm nurses, according to a WIRED and Proof News investigation.
author: Wired

title: FAA Ground Stop Causes Chaotic Hours as Aviation Communications System Instability Persists
content:
The FAA ground stop occurred when instability in the complex US aviation communications system caused chaotic hours for air traffic controllers and pilots.  

Nearly a week later, officials still do not fully know what happened.
summary: Instability in the US aviation communications system caused chaotic hours for air traffic controllers and pilots. Nearly a week later, officials still do not fully know what happened.
author: Wired

title: Cincinnati Zoo’s 9‑year‑old hippo Fiona dies after ingesting a knit hat
content: Fiona, the 9‑year‑old hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo who was celebrated for surviving a premature birth, has died after ingesting a knit hat. Veterinary experts note that even a 2,500‑pound animal can succumb to complications from consuming such an object.
summary: Fiona, a 9‑year‑old hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, died after eating a knit hat. Veterinary experts said the 2,500‑pound animal could succumb to complications from the hat, noting she was known for surviving a premature birth.
author: Wired

title: Walgreens Photo Coupons Offer Up to 70% Off Premium Wall Decor and More This November 2026
content: Walgreens is offering coupons that can save up to 70 % on premium wall decor, stationery, and personalized gifts, as well as beauty, lenses, and health products during the fall season. Customers can apply a verified Walgreens coupon code to receive these discounts.
summary: A verified Walgreens coupon code provides discounts of up to 70% off premium wall decor, stationery, and personalized gifts. The coupons also apply to beauty, lenses, and health products during this fall.
author: Wired

title: Sonos Launches Black Friday Sale: Up to 30% Off Speakers and Soundbars
content:
Sonos has launched its Black Friday sale, offering discounts on a range of speakers and soundbars through November 30. The promotion includes price reductions from Sonos, Amazon, and Best Buy, with savings highlighted for each product.

The Arc Ultra soundbar is available for $849, a $250 discount from its original price. The model supports Dolby Atmos, adds Bluetooth connectivity, and features a Quick Tune function that uses built‑in microphones to adjust audio automatically for the room. It can be paired with a Sonos subwoofer such as the Sub 4, which is part of a bundle priced at $1,499, a $499 discount. The Arc Ultra’s price is listed at $1,099 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $849 at Amazon.

The second‑generation Sonos Beam has a new low price of $339, a $160 discount. It supports Dolby Atmos and HDMI eARC, and can fill a room with rich, clear audio. The Beam’s price is $499 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $339 at Amazon.

For those seeking a smart speaker, the Era 100 SL is offered at $149, a $40 discount. The SL model lacks a built‑in mic, so it does not support voice controls, but it delivers stereo sound with dual tweeters and a large woofer. The standard Era 100 is available for $179 at Amazon and Best Buy. Both models are priced at $189 at Sonos.

The portable Sonos Play is available for $239, a $60 discount. It offers up to 24 hours of battery life, an IP67 rating, and a removable carrying loop. The Play supports Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, and can be grouped with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi‑Fi is not available. Its price is $299 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $239 at Amazon.

Finally, the Sonos Ace headphones are discounted to $229, a $120 reduction. The headphones provide powerful, detailed sound, solid noise cancellation, and a transparency mode. They support up to 30 hours of playback on a single charge and include a TV Audio Swap feature that lets users transfer audio from a compatible Sonos soundbar. The Ace is priced at $399 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $229 at Amazon.
summary: Sonos is offering up to 30% off its speakers and soundbars during a Black Friday sale that runs through November 30th. The sale includes discounts on the Arc Ultra soundbar, Sonos Play portable speaker, and Sonos Era 100 SL smart speaker.
author: The Verge

title: Instagram‑Amazon Affiliate Integration Sparks Creator Skepticism
content:
Instagram announced a new integration with Amazon this month, allowing creators to link their accounts and automatically tag products with affiliate links. This feature enables influencers to earn commissions when followers purchase tagged items, with limits of up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed post. The update aims to simplify a process that previously required influencers to use various workarounds to share affiliate links on social media.

Despite the convenience offered by the new tool, some content creators remain skeptical about the program. These individuals are questioning who ultimately benefits from the integration, expressing suspicion regarding the advantages of the new affiliate structure for influencers.
summary: Instagram announced a new integration with Amazon that lets creators link products to their affiliate accounts. Some influencers question who benefits, as the feature allows up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed.
author: The Verge

title: US IT Outages: How to Tell Cyberattacks from Accidental Failures
content:
Over the past week, a series of high‑profile IT disruptions rattled U.S. infrastructure. A mass Microsoft Exchange outage shut down services for thousands of companies. A Federal Aviation Administration technical error grounded planes nationwide. Software problems at JPMorgan Chase triggered further disruption, while a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights again. An NSA classified network experienced downtime, leaving staff at Fort Meade waiting to return to their offices.

These incidents, occurring on four consecutive business days, coincided with a U.S. war with Iran and growing concerns about AI‑enabled hacking. Observers saw the sequence as more than mere coincidence, but no evidence has surfaced linking the failures to one another or to malicious actors.

Cybersecurity analysts, along with reporters at WIRED, are tasked with distinguishing accidental outages from potential cyberattacks. The article emphasizes that, despite the timing and context, the incidents remain unexplained and have not been proven to be the result of hacking.
summary: Over the past week, major IT services—including Microsoft Exchange, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, and an NSA classified network—experienced outages. Analysts must determine whether these incidents were accidental or the result of cyberattacks.
author: Ars Technica

title: NASA's Artemis Shakeup Adds Burden to Orion Spacecraft
content:
NASA has announced a major revision to its Artemis program that will alter how astronauts reach the Moon. The changes are aimed at giving the agency’s lunar lander partners—SpaceX’s Starship and Blue Origin’s Blue Moon—greater flexibility in their lunar missions.

Under the new plan, Starship will dock with NASA’s Orion spacecraft while still in Earth orbit and then travel to the Moon together. For Blue Moon, the rendezvous with Orion will be moved from Earth orbit to low‑lunar orbit. These adjustments are designed to benefit the landers but place additional demands on Orion, which Lockheed Martin builds for NASA.

To explain the implications for the Orion vehicle, Ars interviewed Kirk Shireman, Human Spaceflight Exploration and Orion program manager at Lockheed Martin.
summary: NASA's Artemis program changes allow SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin Blue Moon to dock with Orion in Earth orbit and low‑lunar orbit, respectively. These adjustments ease lander operations but increase the load on Orion, built by Lockheed Martin, according to program manager Kirk Shireman.
author: Ars Technica

title: Meta’s AI agent Muse mixes up conversations and may expose private data
content: A report claims Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data. Employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that did not belong to them.
summary: Employees reported that Meta’s AI agent Muse displayed messages about childcare requests they never made. The agent also showed career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that did not belong to them.
author: TechCrunch

title: Fireworks AI Co-Founder Advocates Open-Source Models After Anthropic Goes Public
content: On the day Anthropic went public, Fireworks AI’s co‑founder argued that companies could largely avoid expensive models by using open‑source alternatives. He also discussed data breaches that eroded some customers’ trust in the company.
summary: Fireworks AI’s co-founder argued that open source models are a cheaper alternative to pricey AI models. He also addressed breaches that have cost the company some customers’ trust.
author: TechCrunch

title: 15 Tips for Playing Grand Theft Auto VI, Including Fast Walk Setting
content: There’s a vast amount to absorb in Leonida, but these pointers will rev up your criminal engines and allow you to better enjoy the ride Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? Leonida is so huge as to be overwhelming and in the opening hours, the game bombards you with tonnes of info that you will inevitably forget. But I’ve done nothing but play this game for weeks and I’m here to help. Here’s what I wished I’d known at the start Walk faster. I found that Jason and Lucia walk incredibly slowly. If you go into the options menu, you can select “fast walk” as the default walking speed, which sped them up just a little without ruining the pace or atmosphere of the game. While you’re in there, you can also customise plenty of other things, including controls and button mapping.
summary: The article provides 15 tips for navigating the large city of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto VI. One tip advises enabling the “fast walk” option to increase Jason and Lucia’s walking speed and notes that the options menu also allows customization of controls and button mapping.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Parents urged not to buy GTA VI for children due to explicit 18+ content
content:
Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI this week, an 18‑rated title that the author describes as a “criminal caper” filled with sex, drugs and violence. The game is portrayed as a technically sophisticated recreation of a detailed virtual Florida, featuring a central love story between characters named Jason and Lucia, and is said to be both lewd and frequently humorous.

The author recounts a 2014 incident at a stepson’s ninth‑birthday party when a child asked to play Grand Theft Auto V. After refusing, the author explained to the child’s mother that GTA V carried an 18 rating and was not suitable for children. The mother reportedly responded that she had assumed the rating reflected difficulty rather than adult content.

According to the author, Grand Theft Auto VI surpasses previous entries in explicitness, earning its 18 rating more thoroughly than any other game the author has played. The piece emphasizes that the content includes material the author would not want to expose to 10‑ and 7‑year‑old boys. The overall message is a caution to parents against purchasing the game for young children.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI, an 18‑rated game from Rockstar Games released this week, contains explicit sex, drug use and violence. The author urges parents not to purchase the game for their children because of its mature content.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters for GTA VI launch
content:
The new installment of the Grand Theft Auto series, titled GTA VI, launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13‑year development period. The game is described as a Bonnie and Clyde‑inspired crime adventure set in the fictional U.S. state of Leonida.

Following the launch, Grand Theft Auto fans worldwide stayed up through the night, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to play the game, reporting that they were “glued to their screens” while engaging in police chases and coordinated robberies.
summary: Fans worldwide stayed up all night, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to play GTA VI. GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde‑inspired crime adventure set in the fictional state of Leonida, launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13‑year wait.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic lists at $83 per share, above $70‑$78 range, banks earn $550 m fees
content: Can the newly listed AI company really be worth $2tn? Anyone who remembers the late 1990s has good reason to ask Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company. From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees.
summary: Anthropic priced its shares at $83 each, higher than the prospectus range of $70 to $78. The underwriting banks collected $550 million in fees from the offering.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Australian artists protest Labor's AI loophole plan as big tech builds datacentres
content: If the government bends to AI companies, artists, creatives and journalists will be the sacrificial lamb – and Australia will become a global pariah Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Right now, the prime minister faces a choice. Does he stand with Jimmy Barnes and the Working Class Man or does he stand with Big AI? This week, some of the biggest names in Australian music, publishing, journalism and art have thrown down the gauntlet to the government. From Paul Kelly to Anna Funder and Peter Garrett, household names and Australian icons are all singing from the same song sheet.
summary: Paul Kelly, Anna Funder, Peter Garrett and other leading Australian musicians, writers and journalists have publicly challenged the government over Labor's proposed AI loopholes. The article warns that giving AI companies favorable treatment could harm artists, creatives and journalists and could turn Australia into a global pariah.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Athletes increasingly use OnlyFans for income, including Olympic speed skater Bart Swings
content:
A growing number of professional athletes are using the subscription platform OnlyFans to generate additional income. The trend is illustrated by Belgian Olympic speed‑skating champion Bart Swings, who posted an injury update on his OnlyFans channel in August 2025, shortly before the Winter Olympics. The video, which included profanity, was later broadcast on Belgian evening news alongside other regular segments.

OnlyFans, widely known for adult‑oriented content, now lists roughly 285 athletes from sports such as speed skating, rowing, tennis, surfing and golf. While the platform’s reputation is often linked to explicit material, many of the athletes on the service are not sharing adult content, instead using the site for updates and other non‑racy material. The shift reflects a broader move by sports professionals to seek alternative revenue streams beyond their athletic careers.
summary: A growing number of athletes are turning to the subscription platform OnlyFans to earn extra income. The roster, about 285 athletes from sports such as speed skating, rowing, tennis, surfing and golf, includes Belgian Olympic champion Bart Swings, who posted an injury update on his OnlyFans channel, and many are not posting adult content.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic co-founders' stakes valued over $180bn as shares open at $111.50
content:
Anthropic’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela, now hold stakes valued between $26.5bn and $27bn each. This valuation follows the company’s shares opening at $111.50 per share, a price that exceeded expectations and pushed the group’s total paper wealth above $180bn on Thursday. The founding team includes physicists, a former journalist, and an associate of the pope.

The entrepreneurs have pledged to donate 80% of their Anthropic shareholdings to philanthropic causes. At the current share price, this commitment equates to approximately $150bn.
summary: Anthropic co-founders' stakes valued over $180bn as shares open at $111.50.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Putin calls meeting with Trump and Xi a new diplomatic chapter
content: Vladimir Putin says his meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping covered key global security issues, including the war in Ukraine, nuclear proliferation and freedom of navigation. The leaders also discussed maritime law, the role of the International Criminal Court and potential UN reforms.
summary: Vladimir Putin said his meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping covered key global security issues, including the war in Ukraine, nuclear proliferation and freedom of navigation. The leaders also discussed maritime law, the role of the International Criminal Court and potential UN reforms.
author: Euronews

title: Pew study: Islam to be world’s largest religion by 2035, Christianity also expands
content: A Pew Research Center study projects that Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035, while Christianity continues to grow. Between 2020 and 2070 the Muslim population is expected to rise more than 80 % to over 3.6 billion, and the Christian population to increase about 30 % to close to 3 billion.
summary: Pew Research Center projects that Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035. The study forecasts Muslim numbers to rise more than 80% to over 3.6 billion and Christian numbers to increase about 30% to close to 3 billion between 2020 and 2070.
author: Euronews

title: Iraq's PM Ali Faleh al-Zaidi orders Iran-backed group to leave Jurf al-Nasr by Friday
content: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al‑Zaidi has ordered an Iran‑backed group to leave Jurf al‑Nasr by Friday. The directive comes amid alleged oil smuggling and increasing pressure from Washington for Baghdad to place powerful militias under state control.
summary: Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi gave the Iran-backed group until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr. Baghdad is facing growing pressure from Washington to bring powerful militias under state control.
author: Euronews

title: US sells first deep‑sea mining leases off American Samoa despite court ruling
content: The United States sold its first deep‑sea mining leases off American Samoa, a move that came just days after a federal judge ruled that regulators had violated wildlife protection law. Despite the court’s finding, the Trump administration proceeded with the auction, while conservation groups pledged to seek the leases voided.
summary: The Trump administration sold the first deep‑sea mining leases off American Samoa. The sale proceeded days after a federal judge found regulators violated wildlife protection law, and conservation groups said they will seek to void the leases.
author: Euronews

title: Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella posts videos walking among body bags
content: Since taking office in August, Colombia’s far‑right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos of himself walking among body bags that are said to contain the remains of rebel fighters. This communication strategy has sparked widespread criticism in Colombia.
summary: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far‑right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos showing him walking among body bags supposedly holding rebel fighters' remains. The videos have sparked widespread criticism.
author: France 24

title: Voyager 1 reaches one light‑day distance from Earth
content: NASA announced that its Voyager 1 probe, which has been traveling through space for nearly five decades, reached a distance of one light‑day from Earth on Wednesday. The spacecraft, already the most distant human‑made object, is now about 26 billion kilometres (16 billion miles) away, a span that light covers in 24 hours. The milestone was reported by France 24’s Emerald Maxwell.
summary: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, traveling for nearly 50 years, reached a distance of one light‑day from Earth on Wednesday. The spacecraft is now about 26 billion km (16 billion miles) away, the farthest man‑made object, according to NASA.
author: France 24

title: PM Pedro Sanchez admits mistakes in televised debate before Spain election
content: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far‑right Vox party in a position to enter government.
summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said his government had shortcomings during the only televised debate with conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo. The election on November 29 could enable the far‑right Vox party to join the government.
author: France 24

title: White House dismisses national cyber director Sean Cairncross after week of tech outages
content: The White House terminated national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday after a week of technology disruptions that impacted U.S. air travel, email services and national‑security systems. His departure coincides with criticism of the Trump administration’s response to the outages, which officials describe as unrelated incidents.
summary: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday after a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The Trump administration faced criticism over its response to the outages, which officials said were unrelated incidents.
author: France 24

title: UK PM Andy Burnham and EU officials seek trade, youth mobility deals at Brussels summit
content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and senior EU officials will meet in Brussels on Friday to try to seal agreements that would ease trade and expand youth‑mobility programmes. The summit is presented as the first step in Burnham’s effort to rebuild ties with the EU after Brexit.
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and top EU officials are meeting at a Brussels summit on Friday. They hope to seal agreements that would ease trade and improve youth mobility as a first step to rebuild ties after Brexit.
author: France 24

title: Mass protests in Czech Republic oppose Andrej Babiš plan to alter public broadcaster funding
content: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says.
summary: Large demonstrations are challenging Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's proposal to change the funding model of public broadcasters. Mikuláš Minář, chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, warned that the Czech Republic risks democratic backsliding similar to Hungary and Slovakia.
author: France 24

title: Gianni Infantino, Philippe Diallo and Kohzo Tashima officially enter FIFA presidential race
content:
Three candidates have officially submitted bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo is running as an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will be challenged by Japan’s Kohzo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association.  

The FIFA presidential election is scheduled for 18 March 2027 and will be held in Rabat, Morocco.
summary: Gianni Infantino, who has been FIFA president for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo, backed by UEFA, and Japan Football Association honorary president Kohzo Tashima are also candidates, with the election scheduled for March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.
author: France 24

title: Russian attacks kill three, damage two Kyiv bridges, mayor says
content: Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv killed three people and damaged two bridges, city authorities reported on Friday. The attacks occurred after Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged a “painful” retaliation following Ukraine’s recent damage to the Crimea bridge.
summary: Russian attacks on Kyiv killed three people and damaged two bridges, city authorities said on Friday. The attacks came after President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation following Ukraine's damage to the Crimea bridge this week.
author: France 24

title: White House appoints Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies as acting national cyber director
content: The White House announced that Sean Cairncross is leaving his post as national cyber director after a chaotic week of technology outages. The Pentagon’s chief information officer, Kirsten Davies, will step into the role on an acting basis.
summary: Sean Cairncross is leaving his role as national cyber director after a chaotic week of tech outages. Pentagon chief information officer Kirsten Davies will assume the position in an acting capacity.
author: DW World

title: Ukraine allies say Yalta format will not bring peace
content: Berlin meeting of the ‘coalition of the willing’ comes after Trump declared Putin a ‘friend’ during trilateral meeting with Xi in China For what it’s worth, the China-US-Russia ‘peace declaration’ issued after their meeting, and published by Chinese state media, includes absolutely no mention of Ukraine or Europe whatsoever. There is only one, rather generic, line that could be seen as close to these issues: “The three heads of state exchanged in-depth views on the current international situation and pledged to maintain strategic stability and international security.”
summary: Ukraine allies warned that the ‘Yalta format’ will not bring about peace. The warning followed a Berlin meeting of the ‘coalition of the willing’ after Trump called Putin a ‘friend’ at a trilateral summit with Xi in China and a China‑US‑Russia peace declaration that omitted any mention of Ukraine or Europe.

title: UK-EU reset talks will go ‘down to the wire’ as crunch summit approaches
content: Britain makes concessions on youth mobility scheme as negotiations on food and farming go down to the wire British and European negotiators were closing in on a reset deal on Thursday night as they provisionally agreed to allow 100,000 EU citizens to come to the UK every year under a new mobility scheme. It is understood the EU dropped its demands at the last minute that EU students would pay home tuition fees if they attended British universities in a last minute concession to get the deal over the line.

title: Raelene Polymiadis convicted of murdering 94-year-old parents with insulin
content: Jury convicts Raelene Polymiadis after four-month trial in South Australian supreme court Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A jury has convicted a diabetic woman of murdering both her elderly parents with insulin after a marathon criminal trial. Raelene Polymiadis, 66, will face two mandatory life sentences after jurors on Friday delivered unanimous verdicts after a four-month South Australian supreme court trial.
summary: A South Australian Supreme Court jury found 66‑year‑old Raelene Polymiadis guilty of murdering her 94‑year‑old parents using insulin. She faces two mandatory life sentences after the four‑month trial.
author: Guardian World

title: NextDC pledges no new datacentres near homes after Melbourne community backlash
content:
NextDC announced that it will no longer pursue new datacentre developments near residential areas after a community backlash in inner Melbourne. Chief executive Craig Scroggie said public expectations around datacentres have shifted in the age of AI, and the company’s share price fell 40% following the protest‑driven opposition to its expansion plan.

The backlash forced a delay to the expansion of NextDC’s M3 site in West Footscray, after power provider Jemena paused work on new 22‑metre power poles amid community protest. The company said the experience will change how it engages with communities.
summary: NextDC announced it will no longer pursue new datacentre developments near homes after community backlash in inner Melbourne. The backlash, which saw its share price fall 40%, forced a delay to the M3 site expansion in West Footscray after power provider Jemena paused construction of new 22‑metre power poles.

title: Court hears Beau Lamarre-Condon's body disposal explanations ring hollow
content: Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in February 2024 Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Beau Lamarre-Condon knew he had murdered two men and his attempts to explain the disposal of their bodies “ring completely hollow”, a court has heard. Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

title: NSW inquest: four babies died after free or home births; checks might have saved them
content: Inquest into the deaths of four babies after free and home births hears routine checks and follow-up may have saved their lives Four babies who died in New South Wales – three after free births and one after a home birth – might have survived if they had had routine checks and follow-up, a coronial inquest has heard. Baby DH, Baby D, Baby R, and Baby B died in the state’s northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024.
summary: A coronial inquest in New South Wales examined the deaths of four babies—Baby DH, Baby D, Baby R and Baby B—who died in the northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024 after free or home births. The inquest heard that routine checks and follow‑up might have saved the infants.
author: Guardian World

title: UN security council vote may block Costa Rican frontrunner Rebeca Grynspan for secretary‑general
content: Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations. Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.
summary: A vote on Friday could show whether major powers will block the Costa Rican candidate, sparking renewed debate over P5 dominance. Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider, has led all but one of eight straw polls among the 15 council members since the first secret ballot on 30 July.

title: Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
content: At a hearing on the possibility of parole, Smith said she wished she could change the past, and her two children "did not deserve to die".
summary: Susan Smith was denied parole again at a hearing, 32 years after she drowned her two sons. She said she wished she could change the past and that her children did not deserve to die.
author: BBC World

title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
content:
On Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Empire State Building in New York City illuminated its facade in gold to mark a significant milestone for NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft. The golden glow served as a tribute to the Golden Record carried by both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2. The celebration coincided with the moment on November 18, 2026, at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), when Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light-day from Earth.

At this point, the spacecraft is approximately 16 billion miles, or 26 billion kilometers, away from Earth. This distance means that it now takes a full day, or 24 hours, for a light particle to travel from Earth to the probe. Consequently, any signal sent to Voyager 1 or received from it now requires a full day to traverse the gap as the spacecraft continues its exploration of interstellar space.

The Empire State Building was not the only landmark participating in the commemoration. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, along with the Willis Tower and Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois, also lit up in gold to honor the achievement. This multi-city display highlighted the historical significance of Voyager 1 as the farthest human-made object in history.

The Golden Record referenced by the buildings acts as an inanimate ambassador for Earth. It contains information about humanity, our planet, other species, languages, and music, and even includes instructions for constructing a record player. While the Voyager mission has made scientific discoveries throughout the solar system and interstellar space, the record provides a cultural connection to potential unknown life forms. If extraterrestrial life were to encounter Voyager in the distant future, the record might offer them insights into Earth.
summary: The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City.
author: Space.com

title: Saturn will appear near the Moon in the U.S. sky on Nov. 20
content:
On November 20, observers in the United States will have the opportunity to view Saturn positioned close to the moon in the southeastern sky after sunset. The ringed planet will appear more than five degrees from the 82%-lit moon, a distance roughly equivalent to the width of three middle fingers held at arm's length. This alignment offers a naked-eye display accompanied by the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkling nearby.

While moonlight may obscure fainter stars, viewers should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz, and Scheat arranged in a diamond formation above the lunar disk. This asterism marks out the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky. The moon itself will present a target for telescope observation, with the terminator line separating night from day creeping closer to its western edge.

For those using a 6-inch telescope, the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum will be a notable feature. During the moon's waxing gibbous phase, the crater’s eastern rim and central peaks cast intense shadows across its interior. Shifting the telescope to Saturn reveals details in the gas giant's cloud surface and its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Viewers with suitable conditions may also observe Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea, and Iapetus as bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk. The article also highlights the Celestron NexStar 8SE as a recommended motorized telescope for those interested in viewing solar system planets, and invites readers to submit their planetary astrophotography to Space.com.
summary: The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.
author: Space.com

title: Vaonis Vespera Pro Smart Telescope $400 Off, Only 8 Units Left
content:
The price of the original Vaonis Vespera Pro smart telescope has been reduced ahead of Black Friday, which is scheduled for November 27. The discount brings the cost of the device to $2,549 on Amazon, representing a savings of over $400 off its usual retail price of $2,990. This price drop follows the release of the newer Vaonis Vespera Pro 2. According to the source, only eight units of the original model remain in stock, and the article notes that suppliers are expected to run down their remaining inventory of the first version as the new model takes over.

The Vaonis Vespera Pro is described as a portable smart telescope designed for both beginners and professional astrophotographers. It features a 12MP sensor, specifically identified as a 12.5 MP Sony IMX676 sensor that can reach up to 50 MP via CovalENS live mosaic. The device includes 225GB of internal storage, a built-in hygrometer for dew control, and comes with an adjustable tripod and a hard case. Its optical system consists of 50mm aperture quadruplet apochromatic optics. The telescope is controlled through the Singularity app, which contains a database of over 4,000 objects.

In a full review, the Vaonis Vespera Pro received a rating of 4.5 out of 5 stars. The review highlighted the model’s ease of use, intuitive app, and excellent optics. The source states that the telescope is capable of producing high-quality images, noting that the reviewer successfully captured the M81 and M82 galaxies in Ursa Major and the Hercules globular cluster (M13) using the boosted resolution sensor. The design is noted for its portability, making it suitable for use in backyards or at dark sky sites.

The article advises that this deal is suitable for buyers with a larger budget who prefer not to purchase the latest Vaonis Vespera Pro 2, which costs $2,990. Conversely, it suggests that individuals seeking a smart telescope on a smaller budget might consider the Dwarflab Dwarf Mini or the ZWO Seestar S30 Plus instead. The current price of $2,548 is noted as the lowest for this model since March, when it was available for $2,450. The source positions this as an early Black Friday opportunity to acquire pro-level equipment at a reduced cost before the stock of the original model is replaced by the newer release.
summary: The Vaonis Vespera Pro smart telescope is on sale for $2,549, a discount of over $400 from its usual $2,990 price. Only eight units remain in stock, offering buyers a chance to purchase the upgraded 12MP sensor, 225GB storage, and built‑in hygrometer model before it is replaced by the new Vespera Pro 2.
author: Space.com

title: Japan's Hayabusa makes first-ever liftoff from asteroid Itokawa
content:
On November 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft achieved the first-ever liftoff from the surface of an asteroid. The probe had previously descended to a point just 56 feet above asteroid Itokawa before going silent for three hours. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it subsequently lifted off for a second attempt. During this process, the spacecraft bounced off the surface several times and spent approximately 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, though the samplers did not fire.

The primary goal of the Hayabusa mission was to collect samples from an asteroid and return them to Earth, rather than simply achieving a liftoff. Launched by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) on May 9, 2003, the probe originally planned to arrive at Itokawa in early summer 2005. However, a solar storm degraded the spacecraft’s solar arrays, limiting power for its ion engines and delaying the arrival until September 12, 2005. Hayabusa dropped a small lander that was lost and a landing target marker, eventually touching down about 99 feet from the marker.

Following the first landing, the spacecraft entered safe mode, leaving controllers uncertain if any material had been gathered. Despite this uncertainty, they sent the spacecraft back to Earth. A second landing occurred on November 26, 2005. Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, noted that there was no way to confirm if material made it inside the collector after the thrashing on the surface.

Hayabusa’s sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010, touching down in Australia. In November 2010, JAXA announced that scientists found 1,500 dust grains from Itokawa inside the capsule. These samples were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite the collector mechanism not firing, proving that the spacecraft did indeed capture material.

The success of the Hayabusa mission spurred the creation of a follow-up sample-return mission, Hayabusa2. This probe launched in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020. Currently, Hayabusa2 is on an extended mission to fly by asteroid 2015 BM510 in April 2028. It had previously planned to land on asteroid 1998 KY26, but engine trouble made that rendezvous impossible.
summary: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft became the first to liftoff from the surface of asteroid Itokawa after making two touchdowns. The mission successfully returned 1,500 dust grains to Earth in June 2010, proving it captured samples despite the collector mechanism not firing.
author: Space.com

title: Ken Regan releases book of unseen 1985 Madonna photos
content:
Photographer Ken Regan has released Madonna Into the Groove: An Intimate Portrait of the Queen of Pop, a 160-page hardback featuring previously unseen images from his 1985 archive. The book includes biographical text by journalist Tomás Mier and presents the musician at her most vibrant.

The collection offers a behind-the-scenes look at Madonna during the peak of her powers, with the majority of the photographs having never been published before. The images were captured on a single February day in Los Angeles, documenting the artist in an off-duty setting.
summary: Photographer Ken Regan has released a 160-page hardback titled Madonna Into the Groove featuring never-before-seen images from 1985. The book includes biographical text by journalist Tomás Mier and shows the musician in Los Angeles.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Rob Reiner’s JFK assassination book released a year after his death
content:
Rob Reiner, the late director, completed the prologue for his book Who Killed JFK? on 8 December last year, just six days before he and his wife, Michelle Reiner, were stabbed to death in their home. The book, co-authored with David Hoffman and Dick Russell, was based on Reiner’s podcast with Soledad O’Brien and explored his lifelong fascination with the events of 22 November 1963. In the prologue, Reiner described what he viewed as a vast conspiracy to cover up who killed the 35th president, writing, “Maybe, people don’t truly want an answer. Perhaps we are safer not knowing … Well, I’m done being safe.”

The book’s revelation comes a year after the director’s death. Nick Reiner, Rob and Michelle’s son, has been charged with murder in connection with the killings and has pleaded not guilty. The publication offers a final glimpse into Reiner’s perspective on the assassination, highlighting his decision to pursue the truth despite his belief that some may prefer to remain in the dark.
summary: Rob Reiner, the late director, co‑authored the book "Who Killed JFK?" with David Hoffman and Dick Russell, based on his podcast with Soledad O’Brien. Six days after signing the prologue, Reiner and his wife Michelle were stabbed to death in their home, and their son Nick Reiner has pleaded not guilty to the murder charge.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Haruki Murakami's Essay 'Abandoning a Cat' Explores Estranged Father and Childhood Cat
content:
Haruki Murakami’s new book, Abandoning a Cat, expands upon an essay originally published in the New Yorker in 2019. The work is now available as a book and audiobook, translated by Philip Gabriel and narrated by Kotaro Watanabe. The narrative centers on the life and legacy of Murakami’s father, from whom the author was estranged for 20 years and who remained a mystery to him during his lifetime.

The text opens with a childhood memory from Nishinomiya, Japan, where Murakami’s father decided to abandon their cat. He took his son and the cat on a bicycle ride to a beach 2km from their home, leaving the animal in a box among trees before cycling away without looking back. Upon returning home, they discovered the cat had already beaten them back, greeting them with a friendly meow. This incident, along with the father’s decision to banish the pet, represents one of several unanswered questions explored in the essay.

Beyond the cat story, the book delves into the father’s personal history, including his adoption, abandonment, and experiences during the Second World War. Murakami uses these elements to offer an intimate meditation on family dynamics and memory, examining the complex relationship with a parent who was both a source of confusion and a subject of long-term estrangement.
summary: The essay 'Abandoning a Cat' recounts how Murakami's father abandoned a cat during his childhood and the author's later estrangement from his father. It was first published in The New Yorker in 2019 and is now released as a book and audiobook translated by Philip Gabriel and read by Kotaro Watanabe.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Grand Theft Auto unlikely to become TV series, says Take‑Two CEO
content: It is the biggest game of the decade, but there are a billion reasons why GTA shouldn’t be adapted for television. It joins a list of wildly popular titles that won’t see the light of day on streaming platforms You probably aren’t going to see a Grand Theft Auto TV show anytime soon. Speaking on a recent podcast, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of the game’s parent company Take-Two Interactive, said that a film or television adaptation of GTA would only happen if its team thought that it would “somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that. And, of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.” And, well, good. There are a billion reasons why a small screen version would be a terrible idea. Creatively, the thrill of a GTA game is that no two players have the exact same experience. While you might spend your days mowing down civilians and bazookaing police helicopters out of the skies, someone else might take that time to go hiking or explore the waterways. The game is so open-ended, and so moulded to a player’s sensibility, that trying to reduce it to a scripted linear narrative would make it feel uncomfortably thin.
summary: Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take‑Two Interactive, said a Grand Theft Auto film or television adaptation would only happen if it could engage and delight consumers. He added that the game’s open‑ended, player‑specific experience makes it difficult to reduce to a scripted linear narrative, so the company remains very selective.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jimmy Kimmel jokes about Trump’s Apec meeting with Xi and Putin
content: Jimmy Kimmel and other late‑night hosts laughed at Donald Trump’s friendly meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit. They also mocked the administration’s muddled response to various tech outages.
summary: Jimmy Kimmel commented on Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin at the Apec summit. He and other late‑night hosts mocked the meeting and the administration’s response to tech outages.
