title: Launch HN: Onlook (YC W25) – An open-source developer tool for designers
content: Hey HN, I'm Daniel, founder of Onlook ( https://github. Com/onlook-dev/onlook and onlook. Com). Onlook is a desktop app that puts a canvas on top of your real codebase, letting you design directly in code with the agent you already use. Over 25,000 designers and developers have supported the project, 100+ have contributed, and it's been the #1 trending repo in the world twice. We just rebuilt the entire product as an agentic design tool, and open-sourced it to the community. Here’s a demo video: ( https://youtu. Be/BogcYWf4siM ) If you're an engineer, traditional engineering tools are largely built for convergence, whereas designers tend to explore and diverge on ideas. Onlook gives designers a familiar canvas while managing all of the dev processes that get between them and making mind-blowing designs in code. Designers can work on a multiple simultaneous worktrees that run on the real app locally, and every change lands as a PR you can review or throw away, so there aren’t mockups to rebuild. We built Onlook because we believe there needs to be a developer tool that works the way designers do. More and more, designers are expected to work in code. Designers think by seeing, drafting, arranging variations, using references, and remixing ideas. That’s why the canvas has been the signature feature of design tools because it genuinely is useful for how messy the creative process is. Most of the challenge of using engineering tools for design work is that the first half of starting a project often takes mental bandwidth in of itself (What branch am I on? What page was that last exploration on?) and the second half is constrained by configuring your coded design to present itself (prompting design tools on top of what you’ve built or making temporary navigation for that specific state). Some of you may remember our earlier Show HNs (July 2024: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=40904862, August 2024: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=41390449, May 2025: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=44127653 ). Since then, we built a web version (too early), then a Storybook-native build (a mistake). We noticed that our desktop product from July 2024 was still getting hundreds of downloads a month despite zero promotion, so we decided to rebuild it for the new era of designers working in code. How it works… Onlook shines at exploring tons of ideas at once. Ask it to lay out every flow in your product, show every state of a component, or riff on ten versions of one screen. Your designs all show up side by side on an infinite canvas, with each frame as a real webview running your actual app with real data. Not as a mockup, but the real deal. When we built this editor, we had an epiphany that it could be a new kind of IDE for design. Design tools used to be limited to a proprietary setup or closed schema, but now you can push and pull the medium of code to get whatever result you want, so why not give agents an infinite canvas of browsers and see what they do? It turns out, the agents can figure out how to better present coded work by adjusting the urls of browser frames and arranging and resizing them on the canvas. The concept is simple, but it requires a lot of product thinking. For example, because all of the frames on the canvas share a single browser session, and Chromium only allows six connections per host per session, ten frames of the same app end up fighting over limited connections. So, we had to plan around that, and there are still tons of things we need to do to make the canvas ultra performant. Onlook is an Electron app where you can import a repo from GitHub or upload a local folder. Then, Onlook creates a git worktree, starts your dev server, and has the agent sort out missing dependencies or other requirements. You never open a terminal and everything the agent does is a normal git diff that can go to GitHub as a PR. We inject a small script into each frame that draws selection outlines and reads the page, so that way you can click an element, say "make this a card layout," and the agent knows exactly what "this" is. This time we didn't build our own agent. Onlook runs Claude Code or Codex on your own subscription, and we turn whatever the agent emits into one typed event log and draw the UI from that in our own chat interface. On top of that we give the agent a bespoke set of design-specific tools, from arranging frames on the canvas, to making suggestions, to generating multiple iterations of a selection – which is especially useful because the agent decides how to get the app into a state that you need based on your prompt. We also have our own Artifacts which are quick HTML sketches that live in the editor, but outside your repo. They’re almost like components in other design tools in that they can be carried and edited across every project but are detached from the project with no network access. As an example, you can ask the agent to turn your interface into an Artifact, and use it as a reference for another exploration, or download it as HTML and send it to a coworker as an interactive export of something you have in progress. I frequently go back to the artifacts I’ve made as visual snippets when I need new ideas or need to borrow something that’s already been built. The desktop editor is free (you can download it from our website at onlook. Com) and open source under Apache-2.0, and we'll eventually offer a paid cloud product for teams. We'd love to hear which repos work and which don't, what you try to do on the canvas, and what's missing. We’re so excited for this to be a new way for designers to work in code! The Onlook team (Joel - thebrubaker and Kris - krisodd), and I will be here all day! Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50562320 Points: 78 # Comments: 66
summary: Hey HN, I'm Daniel, founder of Onlook ( https://github. Com/onlook-dev/onlook and onlook.

title: Sila signs $1B-plus deal with Panasonic to supply silicon‑carbon anodes
content: After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US. Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than $1 billion over time. This arrangement also shows how much the politics of batteries have shifted lately. A major part of the financial backing for this factory’s production is a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department. While batteries can be a major tool to help drive the energy transition and cut emissions, right now much of the industry is more focused on geopolitics. Founded in 2011, Sila makes silicon-based anodes for lithium-ion batteries. The big selling point here is the potential to improve energy density—Sila’s anode weighs a fifth as much as the graphite used in anodes today and cuts the volume in half, according to the company. So using this new material enables batteries to pack more energy into the same weight and volume, allowing longer range for EVs, for example. The material can also deliver more power and recharge faster, compared with conventional chemistry. We’ve been following Sila (and its competitors) for years. My colleague James Temple covered the company when its battery first appeared in Whoop fitness wearables in 2021. Things have gotten a lot bigger since then. In 2022, Sila announced plans for a factory in Moses Lake, Washington, and received $100 million from the US Department of Energy, part of a multibillion-dollar round of grants under the Biden administration to support the US battery supply chain. The company opened its factory in September 2025, and it’s already operating. But the deal with Panasonic will help it scale to at least 10 times more production than current levels, says Gene Berdichevsky, the company’s cofounder and CEO. Panasonic has committed to buying tens of thousands of tons of material, Berdichevsky says, though Sila isn’t sharing specific numbers on the total commitment or the price Panasonic is paying. This agreement is Sila’s first mass-market deal and a big one for the United States’ next-generation battery market, which has largely been on the ropes over the past few years. Two billion-dollar battery companies, 24M and ESS Tech, have declared bankruptcy and shut down just in the last year. The glimmer of hope here is tied up with something I’ve been noticing about this industry: the shifting politics. While batteries used to be firmly considered a climate technology, we’ve seen a lot of companies move away from messaging around the clean energy transition and lean into geopolitics. China dominates the battery world and particularly the battery anode market, controlling over 90% of graphite production today. For years, the US has been trying to curb reliance on Chinese batteries, battery materials, and other materials used in crucial technologies, like rare earth metals. But the Trump administration has ramped things up, and earlier this year the US Defense Department committed a $1.4 billion loan to Sila aimed at helping the US face a “significant technology sovereignty challenge,” as a press release put it. Sila’s announcement of the Panasonic deal does mention EVs—but not climate, emissions or the energy transition. Rather, it’s all about American industrialization. (And, of course, a mention that a North American battery supply chain can also help power the AI market.) I asked Berdichevsky about this shift and whether the company holds decarbonization as a priority. “I think the politics of it has shifted around us much more than our motivations have shifted,” he said. “It’s really the energy efficiency that motivates engineers like myself and technologists at our company. And I still think that that’s still at the heart of it.” This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.
summary: After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US. Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Australian team keeps human liver alive 7 weeks; Sila signs $1B battery deal with Panasonic
content:
The weekday newsletter The Download delivers a snapshot of recent developments in technology, covering three headline stories: a record‑setting experiment with a human liver, a billion‑dollar battery supply agreement, and a new index that measures AI hype.

In Australia, researchers have kept a donated human liver alive outside the body for seven weeks, surpassing the previous record of roughly two weeks. The team connected the organ to a system of automated pumps and sensors that supplied nutrients, delivered blood, and removed waste. The experiment, reported by Antonio Regalado, suggests that the approach could open new avenues in biomedical engineering, including repairing damaged organs, growing new ones, and even exploring artificial wombs.

A separate story highlights a significant shift in the U.S. battery market. Sila has signed a contract with Panasonic Energy to supply silicon‑carbon anode material that could be worth more than $1 billion. The deal is intended to help Sila scale production and potentially bring smaller, lighter batteries to market. Casey Crownhart notes that the factory backing this partnership received a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department, underscoring a growing focus on geopolitics within the battery industry.

The newsletter also introduces the AI Hype Index, a tool designed to separate reality from hype in the AI sector. The latest edition tracks AI’s influence across diverse areas—from literary prizes and cyberattacks to a Grok‑ified version of The Odyssey. The index offers a quick snapshot of what is shaping the industry each month, and the newsletter lists several high‑profile AI stories, such as Anthropic’s record‑breaking IPO and China’s pursuit of AI‑powered weapons, as part of its “must‑reads” section.
summary: Researchers in Australia kept a donated human liver alive on a perfusion system for seven weeks, breaking the previous record of about two weeks. Sila announced a deal with Panasonic Energy to supply silicon‑carbon anode material worth more than $1 billion, backed by a $1.4 billion Defense Department loan.

title: FCC votes unanimously to let prisons jam cellphone signals
content:
The Federal Communications Commission voted unanimously on Thursday to permit state and local prisons to jam cellphones. The FCC stated that the new rule aims to address an influx of contraband cellphones used to commit crimes from within prison facilities. Although jamming devices are generally prohibited under Section 333 of the Communications Act of 1934, they are currently utilized in some federal facilities.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr asserted that providing correctional facilities with this technology will prevent prisoners from engaging in illegal activity. He noted that inmates use these devices to order hits, run drug operations, and traffic women.
summary: The Federal Communications Commission voted unanimously on Thursday to allow state and local prisons to jam cellphone signals. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said the rule will help prevent inmates from using phones for illegal activity.

title: Male mice that watch fights learn to defend better, study finds
content:
Scientists have used a mouse model to investigate why humans are drawn to violent entertainment. A recent paper published in Nature reports that male mice that observed other mice fighting performed better when later challenged by stronger opponents than mice that had no such exposure.

In the experiment, researchers divided male mice into three groups: fighters, spectators, and novices. Over eight days, each group received three 10‑minute training sessions per day. Novice mice played with stuffed mice in isolation, while spectator mice watched pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier. This arrangement allowed the spectators to see, smell, and hear the fights.

On the ninth day, all mice faced a “fight night” against a formidable opponent in three 4‑minute rounds. Each bout was filmed from above to allow detailed behavioral analysis.

To track brain activity, the team genetically engineered the mice’s excitatory neurons to glow green when activated and inhibitory neurons to glow red. They also implanted optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions, enabling simultaneous monitoring of activity across the brain during the fights.
summary: Researchers assigned male mice to fighter, spectator or novice groups and gave them eight days of training with three 10‑minute sessions per day. On the test day, spectator mice that had watched other mice fight performed better against a stronger opponent than novice mice, according to a Nature paper.

title: Google to roll out global Android developer verification in January 2027
content:
Google has announced that it will extend its Android developer verification program worldwide in January 2027. The program, introduced last year, already blocks the installation of unregistered apps in several countries this fall and will soon apply to all regions. Developers who have not yet registered are urged to do so before the rollout.

Under the new rule, apps downloaded from the Play Store will continue to come from verified developers, and the requirement will now also cover apps from third‑party sources. When verification is active in a user’s region, sideloading apps will be prohibited unless the developer has registered with Google. Verification requires the submission of government identification and a $25 fee, a measure the company frames as a security improvement.

In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand without major incidents. The company previously indicated a 2027 global rollout and now confirms that the requirement will reach all devices within “several months” of the January start.
summary: Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon.
author: Ars Technica

title: UCL and UNESCO study finds LLMs can give incorrect climate answers when prompted
content:
Many researchers have long examined how people encounter climate science information, focusing on the top results that Google surfaced when it still served links, as well as on social media posts and coverage in newspapers and television. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a significant part of the public information diet, it has become important to understand how these models handle climate‑change content.

A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) sought to address this gap. Because LLM output is delivered ephemerally to individual users and confined to a chat session, there is no direct way for researchers to track the information people have actually seen. The study therefore tested LLMs with a variety of prompts and evaluated their responses.

The researchers began with benchmarks of simple factual questions—questions that might already be present in the models’ training data—and then moved on to more complex interactions, including scenarios where users challenge the model’s answers. The study evaluated 33 different models, covering multiple versions of major frontier and open‑weight models. The flagship frontier models examined were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT‑5.6 Sol. A full list of the models used is provided in the report.
summary: Researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) evaluated 33 large language models on climate‑change queries. Using both simple factual benchmarks and more complex prompts where users push back, the study found the models can provide incorrect climate information.

title: Google to launch data‑center satellites on Blue Origin's New Glenn in 2029
content:

The payload is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, a research initiative that the company described a year ago as a “moonshot” aimed at creating scalable orbiting data centers.

The mission will place satellites, each offering computing capacity comparable to a data‑center rack, into a Sun‑synchronous orbit where they can draw nearly continuous solar power. Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, said the dedicated Blue Origin launch marks a “crucial milestone” as the company seeks to expand AI infrastructure in space by leveraging abundant orbital solar energy.
summary: Blue Origin announced that its New Glenn rocket will launch Google’s Project Suncatcher data‑center satellites to Sun‑synchronous orbit in 2029. Each satellite will have computing capacity roughly equivalent to a data‑center rack and will draw nearly continuous solar power, according to Google senior director Travis Beals.

title: Black teens sue Baltimore County schools, police after AI gun alert misreads Doritos bag
content: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. title: Russian national Igor D’iu indicted for spying on Silicon Valley firm aiding Ukraine
content:
Federal prosecutors have indicted a 25‑year‑old Russian national, Igor D’iu, on suspicion that he acted as a Russian spy targeting a Silicon Valley technology firm that provides assistance to Ukraine. According to the indictment, D’iu photographed employees and their computer screens while they worked in a coffee shop near the company’s Palo Alto office and compiled a list of home addresses for staff members and a senior executive.

The filing also describes an incident in which D’iu followed a female employee, identified in the affidavit as “FEMP1,” as she traveled from Palo Alto to San Francisco. Prosecutors say D’iu pursued her for nearly thirty miles, making evasive turns, running a red light and entering a grocery‑store parking lot before the employee called 911. She was directed to drive to the San Francisco Police Department’s Mission Station, where she flagged a patrol car and reported the chase; D’iu left after police made contact.
summary: Russian national Igor D’iu indicted for spying on Silicon Valley firm aiding Ukraine.
author: Ars Technica

title: Report finds MAHA PAC spent more on steak and luxury club than on candidates
content:
A Stat report examining the finances of the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) political action committee shows that the organization’s spending patterns during the recent midterm election cycle favored non‑candidate expenses. The report, which analyzed the PAC’s financial documents, found that the MAHA PAC, headed by Tony Lyons, allocated more money to allies, boosters, meals, luxury items and its affiliated nonprofit than it did to political candidates.

The spending data contrast with a spring announcement by Lyons that he was leading a $100 million fundraiser intended to increase MAHA’s influence in the midterms. According to the report, the PAC actually raised $3.2 million and spent over $10.5 million in the election cycle, with more than $7 million of that coming from previously collected funds. The findings raise questions about the group’s priorities amid the movement’s broader midterm losses.
summary: Report finds MAHA PAC spent more on steak and luxury club than on candidates.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon uses homepage banner and app pop‑up to oppose NYC Delivery Protection Act
content:
Amazon has placed a vertical banner on its website and a pop‑up within its mobile app warning shoppers that the New York City Council could add up to $5 to each order. The banner, which appears when users are logged in, includes a button labeled “Act now.” A screenshot of the homepage banner was credited to Scharon Harding/Amazon.

According to Bloomberg, the message is intended to persuade shoppers not to support the proposed legislation. Amazon has not disclosed whether the notice is targeted to New York City residents based on account addresses, device location services, or another method. The company’s approach represents an unprecedented use of its consumer platform to address a specific municipal bill.
summary: Amazon is displaying a vertical banner on its website and a pop‑up in its app urging shoppers not to support a New York City bill. The banner warns that the NYC Council could add up to $5 per order and includes an “Act now” button, and Amazon has not explained how it targets users.
author: Ars Technica

title: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia after affair, raising national security concerns
content: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia after an affair, according to the report. The resignation is noted as potentially affecting national security amid the United States and China’s competition to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U. S.
author: TechCrunch

title: Cybersecurity experts link recent airline, banking and productivity platform outages
content: Recent outages have affected airline booking systems, banking platforms and productivity tools. Cybersecurity experts say the simultaneous failures are unlikely to be a coincidence and suggest a deeper underlying issue may be responsible.
summary: Recent outages have impacted airline booking systems, banking platforms and productivity platforms. Cybersecurity experts say the incidents likely have a deeper cause.
author: TechCrunch

title: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk says design of rooftop cell tower completed to end dead zones
content: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company has completed the design of a miniature rooftop cell tower that could provide better coverage to mobile phones and eliminate dead zones.
summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company has completed the design of a miniature rooftop cell tower. The tower could provide better mobile phone coverage and eliminate dead zones.
author: TechCrunch

title: Australian datacentre opposition gains momentum as Wingecaribee council backs moratorium
content:
A network of grassroots campaigners across Australia is sharing information to counter the rapid development of data‑centre projects. Their coordinated efforts aim to inform communities about the environmental and social impacts of new data‑centre infrastructure.

In March, Heather Champion tabled a council motion opposing a large gas plant intended to power a new data‑centre in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales. The motion did not pass.

Five months later, the local councillor for Wingecaribee introduced a new motion urging the federal government to impose a moratorium on new data‑centres. This motion was adopted unanimously by the council.
summary: A network of grassroots campaigners across Australia is sharing information to oppose the datacentre development boom. After Heather Champion's March council motion against a gas plant for a datacentre failed, a Wingecaribee councillor's motion calling for a federal moratorium on new datacentres passed unanimously five months later.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Australian music industry rejects AI carve‑out proposal giving musicians exemption
content: Reported proposal to give musicians special treatment is ‘unworkable’, Aria chief executive says Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The music industry has declared it will not accept an AI carveout deal that leaves other creative sectors behind, rejecting a reported proposal to give musicians special treatment while allowing big tech to train on other copyrighted material – described by David Pocock as a “divide and conquer strategy”. The trade union representing writers and creatives is “alarmed” at a proposal to let AI companies train on Australian data if they buy a permit, an idea also strongly rebuffed by the Coalition and Greens. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
summary: Australia’s music industry said it will not accept a proposal that would exempt musicians from AI scraping while permitting AI companies to train on other copyrighted material. ARIA’s chief executive called the plan unworkable, and the writers’ union, the Coalition and the Greens also voiced opposition.
author: Guardian Technology

title: IMF head warns AI demand will push central banks to raise interest rates
content: Kristalina Georgieva says countries needed to be ready for tech rollout, adding: ‘You snooze, you lose’ Business live – latest updates Booming demand for artificial intelligence will force the world’s most powerful central banks to raise interest rates, the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned. Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the Washington-based fund, said demand for AI hardware and related technology products was pushing up consumer prices around the world.
summary: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva said booming demand for artificial intelligence hardware and related technology is raising consumer prices worldwide. She warned that this pressure will force the world’s most powerful central banks to raise interest rates.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warns of very real AI risks before Nasdaq opening bell
content: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that AI presents “very real” but “avoidable” risks. The comment was made shortly before the company rang the opening bell at Nasdaq, where Anthropic’s shares opened more than 20% higher at over $100 each following its IPO.
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said AI poses "very real" but "avoidable" risks. He made the comment shortly before Anthropic rang the Nasdaq opening bell, where the stock opened more than 20% higher at over $100 a share after its IPO.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Senators letter Apple, Google, Meta over weak nudification app safeguards
content: Exclusive: three Senate Democrats send letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms A trio of US senators says Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect or remove apps meant to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. The senators also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”. On Wednesday, Ron Wyden, Ed Markey and Ben Luján sent letters to the CEOs of the tech companies, saying the safeguards they have in place to keep nudification off their app stores or platforms are not sufficient.
summary: Senators letter Apple, Google, Meta over weak nudification app safeguards.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Waymo halts driverless taxi rides on US freeways after California ban
content:
Waymo, the autonomous‑driving subsidiary of Alphabet, has halted driverless taxi service on freeways across the United States indefinitely. The suspension follows California’s decision to bar the vehicles from its own freeways after recent traffic incidents.  

Before the pullback, Waymo’s robotaxis could be summoned for freeway trips in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The company continues to operate driverless rides on city streets in other markets, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver, which are not affected by the freeway suspension.
summary: Waymo has suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways indefinitely after California banned the vehicles from its freeways. The company continues to offer robotaxi rides on city streets in locations such as Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver, which are not affected by the suspension.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia approaches Arm CEO Rene Haas in search for new CEO
content:
Nvidia’s board has engaged the recruiting firm Heidrick & Struggles to identify a successor after co‑founder Jensen Huang’s exit, and the firm has begun contacting potential candidates, Bloomberg reports.  

Among those approached is Rene Haas, the chief executive of Cambridge‑based chip company Arm, who is being described as a leading contender for Nvidia’s new chief executive role.
summary: Nvidia's board hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a new CEO after Jensen Huang's exit. The recruiter has approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas, who is viewed as a leading contender.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic ends first trading day at $1.3 trillion valuation, shares close near $97
content:
Anthropic, the artificial‑intelligence startup behind the Claude chatbot, completed its initial public offering on Thursday and closed its first day of U.S. trading with a share price just above $97. That price represented a roughly 17 percent increase over the IPO price of $83, giving the company a market capitalization of nearly $1.3 trillion and a fully‑diluted value of about $1.75 trillion.

The stock opened with a 34 percent surge, briefly pushing the implied valuation above $2 trillion and reaching an intraday high of $111.50 per share. By the market close, the price had settled below that peak but remained above the offering level. The debut places Anthropic among the largest stock market flotations in history and makes it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded businesses. The company, founded in 2021, achieved this valuation on its first day of public trading.
summary: Anthropic's shares closed its first day of US trading at just over $97, giving the company a market capitalization of about $1.3 trillion. The price was about 17% above the IPO price of $83 after an initial surge that briefly valued the firm at more than $2 trillion.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump questions Europe's billions in Ukraine aid during surprise Air Force One call
content: U.S. President Donald Trump made a surprise call from Air Force One into a meeting of Kyiv’s European allies, questioning the billions of euros Europe is providing to Ukraine. The call came hours after Trump’s talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, during which he said Moscow was ready to negotiate a peace deal.
summary: President Trump joined a meeting of Kyiv's European allies by phone from Air Force One, hours after talks with Putin and Xi. He said Moscow was ready to negotiate a peace deal and questioned Europe's billions in Ukraine aid.
author: Euronews

title: Euronews aboard Latvian vessel Valpas patrols waters off Crete as Libya migrant arrivals rise
content: Euronews boarded the Latvian patrol vessel Valpas to film maritime operations off Crete as migrant arrivals from Libya increase. The crew also visited a Frontex drone base at Tympaki airfield. A concurrent search for missing migrants near Chrissi Island underscored the crossing’s hazards, while temporary reception facilities reported mounting pressure.
summary: Euronews boarded the Latvian patrol vessel Valpas to follow maritime operations off Crete and visited a Frontex drone base at Tympaki airfield. It also reported a search for missing migrants near Chrissi Island and growing pressure on temporary reception facilities as migrant arrivals from Libya rise.
author: Euronews

title: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion Nasdaq debut sparks protest over AI bubble
content: Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq with a record‑breaking initial public offering that valued the artificial‑intelligence firm at $1.5 trillion. Outside the New York exchange, police detained three protesters who warned that the deal posed financial‑risk concerns.
summary: Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq with an IPO that valued the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Police detained three protesters outside the New York exchange who warned of financial risks.
author: Euronews

title: Trump departs China without meeting Kim Jong-un as US, China, Russia pledge nuclear talks
content: President Donald Trump departed China without meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong‑un. At a trilateral summit, the United States, China and Russia pledged to hold talks on nuclear risk reduction, while their joint peace declaration made no reference to North Korea.
summary: Trump left China without meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The United States, Chinese and Russian leaders pledged to hold talks on nuclear risk reduction but made no mention of North Korea in their joint peace declaration.
author: Euronews

title: Pakistan deputy prime minister says new regional security architecture will benefit Europe
content: In an exclusive interview on Euronews’ World Conversation, Pakistan’s deputy prime minister said that behind‑the‑scenes work contributed to the US‑Israel agreement that ended the war in June. He also described Pakistan’s plan for a new regional security architecture that would be coordinated with Europe and benefit the continent.
summary: In an exclusive interview for Euronews’ World Conversation show, Pakistan’s deputy prime minister discussed the backstage efforts that led to the US‑Israel agreement to end the war in June. He also outlined Pakistan’s strategy for a new regional security architecture coordinated with Europe.
author: Euronews

title: At least one dead and dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal en route to Spain
content: A migrant boat capsized off Senegal while heading toward Spain, leaving at least one person dead and dozens missing. The incident occurred as departures toward the Canary Islands have surged, with more than 11,000 people arriving in the Spanish archipelago during the first two weeks of November.
summary: The latest sinking comes amid a sharp rise in departures towards the Canary Islands, with more than 11,000 people reaching the Spanish archipelago in the first two weeks of November.
author: Euronews

title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth lands in Ecuador on anti‑narcotics tour
content: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth landed in Ecuador as part of a Latin America anti‑narcotics tour. He is under fire for his role in the Iran war and for illegal bombings in the Caribbean and Pacific, and has announced a military pact with Venezuela. His next stop is Honduras.
summary: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth arrived in Ecuador as part of a Latin America anti‑narcotics tour. He announced a military pact with Venezuela and said his next stop will be Honduras.
author: Euronews

title: Macron urges Ukraine allies to speed air defence and reconsider NATO membership
content: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that Ukraine’s allies should accelerate the provision of urgently needed air‑defence systems and should “reopen the question” of Kyiv’s NATO membership. His remarks followed talks in Berlin that were intended to reaffirm European support for Ukraine.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday urged Ukraine's allies to accelerate delivery of urgently needed air defence systems. He also called them to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's NATO membership after talks in Berlin aimed at reaffirming European support for Kyiv.
author: France 24

title: Jared Kushner says Trump open to extending NATO‑like defense guarantee to Ukraine
content: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.
summary: Jared Kushner says Trump open to extending NATO‑like defense guarantee to Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
content: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".
summary: We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says.
author: France 24

title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Austria and Netherlands embassies
content:
A series of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday resulted in the death of one person and caused damage to a historic cathedral and the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. The attacks were part of a broader wave of explosions that erupted across the Ukrainian capital throughout the day.

At the same time, leaders of Russia, China and the United States were holding a historic meeting in China, a gathering that placed Russian President Vladimir Putin in the international spotlight. The report was provided by FRANCE 24’s Laurent Berstecher.
summary: Daytime Russian strikes hit Kyiv on Thursday, killing one person and damaging a historic cathedral. The attacks also damaged the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands.
author: France 24

title: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir receives three-year doping ban
content:
Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for doping.

In South Africa, judges toured a repatriation centre before delivering judgments on 33 emergency asylum applications. Meanwhile, Ghana's presidency has acquired a new jet, though critics of the ruling party are not supportive.
summary: Peres Jepchirchir, a Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion, has been banned for doping. The ban lasts three years.
author: France 24

title: Jean‑Luc Mélenchon signals possible alliance with Greens candidate Marine Tondelier
content: Jean‑Luc Mélenchon, the French far‑left leader, opened the possibility of an alliance with the Greens after Marine Tondelier, the Greens’ presidential candidate, said she was ready to work on a coalition around him. The overture is said to boost Mélenchon’s campaign for the Élysée Palace and has angered moderates on the centre‑left.
summary: French far‑left leader Jean‑Luc Mélenchon said he is open to an alliance with the Greens after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier expressed readiness to work on a coalition around him. The overture has boosted Mélenchon’s campaign for the Élysée Palace and angered moderates on the centre‑left.
author: France 24

title: Anthropic's IPO lifts stock 17% but Wall Street indexes fall
content:
Anthropic has become the first pure‑play AI developer to be publicly traded on the stock market, following a record‑setting IPO.  

The stock opened 34 % higher, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion, before ending its first day of trading up 17 %.  

Wall Street indexes closed sharply lower as investors took profits, reflecting underlying market jitters about the AI trade.
summary: Anthropic became the first pure‑play AI developer to trade publicly after a record‑setting IPO that opened 34% higher and briefly valued the company at over $2 trillion. The stock closed its first day up 17% while Wall Street indexes ended sharply lower as investors took profits.
author: France 24

title: Haitian security forces' anti-gang offensive kills 34 suspected gang members
content: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port‑au‑Prince with the country’s western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.
summary: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.
author: France 24

title: International Court of Justice upholds genocide ruling against Myanmar over Rohingya
content:
The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority.  

The court called for Myanmar to pay reparations and to allow refugees to return safely.
summary: The International Court of Justice upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. The court ordered Myanmar to pay reparations and allow refugees to return safely.
author: DW World

title: Pakistani Minister Visits India for SCO Forum, No Bilateral Resumption Expected
content:
A Pakistani minister will visit India for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization forum, marking a rare high‑level contact between the archrivals.  

Analysts say the visit does not signal a resumption of bilateral engagement.
summary: A Pakistani minister visited India for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization forum, marking a rare high‑level contact between the archrivals. Analysts say the visit does not signal a resumption of bilateral engagement.
author: DW World

title: FM Wadephul says Berlin 'Coalition of the Willing' meeting sends strong signal to Moscow
content: German Foreign Minister Wadephul said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.
summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He warned that Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.
author: DW World

title: European Commission says it was hit by AI-generated cybercampaign
content: The European Commission confirmed it was targeted by an “AI‑generated cybercampaign,” according to a spokesperson. This marks the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI‑based cyberattack.
summary: The European Commission was targeted by an AI-generated cybercampaign, a spokesperson said. It is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.
author: DW World

title: China, US and Russia presidents hold unprecedented trilateral summit
content: China’s President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin recently convened an unprecedented trilateral summit. Trump remarked that the three leaders were “making history,” while Xi called the talks “fruitful” and Putin described them as “open and candid.” The meeting marked a rare gathering of the three heads of state.
summary: The presidents of China, the United States and Russia held an unprecedented summit. Trump said the leaders were making history, Xi called the talks fruitful and Putin described them as open and candid.
author: DW World

title: Iraqi security forces surround Kataib Hezbollah area in risky standoff
content: Iraqi security forces this week surrounded a location controlled by the Kataib Hezbollah militia. Observers said the action represented the most dangerous confrontation in decades between the Iraqi state and Iran‑aligned militias.
summary: This week, Iraqi security forces surrounded an area run by the Kataib Hezbollah militia. Onlookers describe it as the most dangerous confrontation between the Iraqi state and Iran-allied militias in decades.
author: DW World

title: Putin proposes evacuation of Kostiantynivka, experts warn it may be a military trap
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, mirroring the recent operation in Oleshky.  

Experts caution that the move may serve military objectives rather than humanitarian ones.
summary: Russian President Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, similar to the recent operation in Oleshky. Experts warn that the evacuation could serve military rather than humanitarian aims, raising questions for Kyiv.
author: DW World

title: ICJ rules Myanmar responsible for genocide against Rohingya
content: The International Court of Justice, the United Nations’ principal judicial organ, issued its judgment on Thursday in The Gambia v. Myanmar under the Genocide Convention. The court found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, marking the first ruling of its kind against a state.
summary: The International Court of Justice delivered its judgment on Thursday in The Gambia v. Myanmar under the Genocide Convention. The court found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.
author: UN News

title: UN Human Rights Committee says government approval not required to form or join groups
content: The UN Human Rights Committee announced on Thursday that individuals do not require their government’s permission to form or join an association, issuing new guidance amid a global contraction of civic space.
summary: On Thursday, the UN Human Rights Committee said people do not need their government’s permission to form or join an association. The committee issued new guidance as civic space shrinks around the world.
author: UN News

title: COP31 cat Ambition missing as draft drops fossil fuel language
content:
A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday, a moment activists highlighted with humour. The incident underscored their concern that explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels have disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement.

On the eve of the summit’s scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still working to bridge sharp differences, while civil‑society groups continued to press for stronger action on the fossil‑fuel issue.
summary: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday, prompting activists to use humour to highlight concerns. The latest draft climate agreement omitted explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels, and ministers and the Presidency were still negotiating differences as civil society groups called for stronger action.
author: UN News

title: Guardian Australia wins two Walkley awards for Hanson‑Rinehart trip and Lomas story
content:
Guardian Australia journalists have won two Walkley awards.  

One award was for a story about the systemic betrayal of a woman who was killed by her partner, and the other was for an exclusive story that revealed Pauline Hanson had travelled to the US with mining billionaire Gina Rinehart.  

Investigative reporter Sarah Martin won the award for print/text news report for her exclusive story that revealed the One Nation leader and her chief of staff, James Ashby, travelled with Rinehart on the mining magnate’s Gulfstream 700 on 27 October last year.
summary: Guardian Australia wins two Walkley awards for Hanson‑Rinehart trip and Lomas story.
author: Guardian World

title: Mark Speakman quits, warns Liberal Party of existential threat amid NSW MP exodus
content: Former NSW opposition leader warns party against becoming ‘Labor lite’ or ‘One Nation lite’ in late-night speech Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Former New South Wales opposition leader Mark Speakman will not contest his seat at the March state election, the latest in a mass exodus of MPs under the Liberal leader who replaced him, Kellie Sloane. In a late-night speech on Thursday, the final sitting day of NSW’s legislative assembly before the vote, Speakman said he would not contest his south Sydney seat of Cronulla, which he has held since 2011.
summary: Mark Speakman quits, warns Liberal Party of existential threat amid NSW MP exodus.
author: Guardian World

title: Former Liberal minister Sharman Stone dies by voluntary assisted dying at 75
content:
Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone died via voluntary assisted dying at age 75 on Wednesday, surrounded by family, after a long battle with glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer.  

Stone’s political career included serving as minister for workforce participation from 2006‑07 and as ambassador for women and girls from 2016‑20, during which she advocated that people should have autonomy over their bodies.
summary: Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone died at age 75 via voluntary assisted dying after a long battle with glioblastoma, surrounded by family. She had served as minister for workforce participation from 2006‑07 and as ambassador for women and girls from 2016‑20.
author: Guardian World

title: UQ physicists send word ‘gravity’ through brick wall via elevator
content:
Australian physicists at the University of Queensland demonstrated a proof‑of‑concept experiment in which they transmitted the word “gravity” in binary code through a brick wall. The experiment used a slow‑moving 1950s‑era elevator, a brick wall and a men’s bathroom as part of the setup.  

By moving the elevator up and down between two floors, the team measured the resulting changes in the gravitational field. The variations in gravity were used to encode a “practically unblockable” message that traveled approximately 70 cm through the brick wall. The demonstration shows that gravity can be used as a means of communication in a controlled laboratory setting.
summary: Australian physicists at the University of Queensland conducted a proof‑of‑concept experiment using a 1950s elevator to transmit the word “gravity” in binary through a brick wall. The method measured changes in the gravitational field over about 70 cm as the elevator moved between two floors, creating a “practically unblockable” message.
author: Guardian World

title: Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen, summit called historic but yields little
content: Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”. But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “new page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century.
summary: Leaders of China, Russia and the United States gathered for the first time in Shenzhen. While Vladimir Putin said the meeting wrote a new page in diplomatic history, analysts say it produced few tangible outcomes and will be a footnote.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump accused of sleeping during Xi Jinping's APEC summit speech in China
content:
The United States president was accused of falling asleep while Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered his speech at the Asia‑Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. Observers noted that Trump’s eyes were closed for roughly ten seconds on Thursday, his head tilted downward and his hands remained clasped in front of him.  

The White House responded to the claim by insisting that the president was awake during the televised event. No further details were provided.
summary: Donald Trump was accused of falling asleep while Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered his speech at the APEC summit in China. The White House said he was awake, noting his eyes were closed for about 10 seconds with his head tilted downward and his hands clasped.
author: Guardian World

title: China, Russia and US issue peace declaration that omits Ukraine and Iran wars
content:
China’s President Xi Jinping, Russia’s President Vladimir Putin and the United States’ President Donald Trump said they had reached a peace declaration after an unprecedented trilateral summit. The statement, issued on Thursday, did not refer to the wars in Ukraine or Iran that involve two of the participants.  

The declaration outlined three priorities: reform of the United Nations, measures to boost oil supplies and a commitment to the protection of diplomatic immunity.
summary: China, Russia and the United States issued a peace declaration after an unprecedented trilateral summit. The Thursday declaration listed priorities including UN reform, boosting oil supplies and protecting diplomatic immunity, and made no mention of the wars in Ukraine or Iran.
author: Guardian World

title: South Africa moves to replant five centuries‑old baobabs after illegal export halted
content:
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries‑old baobabs after an export attempt was blocked. The 20‑tonne trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were dug up by an exporter without the required permits and were to be shipped thousands of miles to the U.S. state.  

The trees arrived at a reserve in Timbavati in north‑eastern South Africa on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to aid recovery. They had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July after authorities intercepted them for lacking the necessary permissions.
summary: Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries‑old baobab trees after they were dug up by an exporter without permits. The trees arrived at a reserve in Timbavati on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables after being stranded in a Durban warehouse since July when authorities intercepted them.
author: Guardian World

title: Wales upset All Blacks in Cardiff, sparking hope for rank outsiders
content: The plot twist in Cardiff that nobody saw coming suggests the northern hemisphere is remobilising in time for next year’s World Cup What does it take to beat the All Blacks in Cardiff? “I’ll never forget the pressure they put us under. I don’t think we were a better team than New Zealand, but there was a certain spirit in the Welsh side which pulled us through.” The vivid recollections of the late, great Cliff Morgan on Wales’s famous victory in 1953 could just as easily have applied to the long-awaited modern-day sequel on Saturday. Seventy-three years. The last time it came to pass was the year Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay officially became the first people to conquer Everest. Some bookmakers had even stopped taking bets on an All Blacks win; in the buildup the Wales side were likened in one New Zealand newspaper to “Dickensian orphans” begging for scraps. More bread of heaven, please sir? Here was a plot twist nobody saw coming.
summary: Wales achieved a surprise victory over the All Blacks in Cardiff. The result is being viewed as a sign that the northern hemisphere is remobilising ahead of next year’s World Cup, giving rank outsiders fresh hope.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emma Hayes names USWNT squad for Concacaf Championship and World Cup qualifier
content:
Emma Hayes has named a veteran squad for the United States women’s national team’s upcoming Concacaf W Championship and World Cup qualifier. The team is set to begin its campaign on November 27 against El Salvador. Hayes, who has tested fresh faces and new combinations over the past two years since the Paris Olympics, has expanded her roster options to 61 players, with 33 earning their first caps under her leadership.

The squad announcement includes the return of Sam Coffey after an injury absence, while Naomi Girma will miss the tournament due to injury. The primary objective for the USWNT is to defeat El Salvador in the quarter-final match. A victory in this game would secure the team’s qualification for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.

While the United States has won the Concacaf W Championship in nine of the tournament’s 11 previous installments, the immediate focus remains on overcoming El Salvador. Failing to win the quarter-final would force the team to rely on a playoff to reach next summer’s World Cup.
summary: Emma Hayes selected a veteran group for the Concacaf W Championship, noting that Naomi Girma is absent due to injury while Sam Coffey returns. A victory over El Salvador on November 27 would secure US qualification for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Janine van Wyk recalls empty rooms and lack of water at 2006 Wafcon
content:
Janine van Wyk, the former South Africa captain, has shared an extract from her book detailing the challenging preparations for the 2006 Women’s African Football Championship (Wafcon) in Nigeria. Van Wyk, who was only one year into her international career, described the team’s initial excitement and nervousness, particularly after being drawn in the same group as the hosts. The tournament, then known as the African Women’s Championship, saw South Africa secure victories against Algeria and Equatorial Guinea before facing Nigeria in a decisive group-stage match in Delta State.

The former captain highlighted the difficulties of traveling to Nigeria, a country she noted was reputed to be the toughest for South Africans to visit. She referenced the well-known rivalry between the two nations, which extends beyond the football field. Van Wyk’s account underscores the logistical and interpersonal challenges the team faced during this early stage of her career, providing insight into the conditions under which the squad prepared for their crucial encounter with the Nigerian hosts.
summary: Former South Africa captain Janine van Wyk describes the poor accommodations her team faced during the 2006 African Women’s Championship in Nigeria. She details how the team's rooms lacked mattresses, lightbulbs, and water before a decisive match against the hosts.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino's USMNT tenure improved culture but lacked transformational impact
content: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville.
summary: The incoming Manchester United manager enhanced the US team's culture and competitiveness during his two-year tenure. However, he was unable to bring about a sea change in the team's performance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Professor uses cricket metaphor to explain memory errors in Sandpapergate
content: One of Pat Cummins or Usman Khawaja must be lying about Cape Town? Not so, says a professor of memory In 1932, the English psychologist Frederic Bartlett used cricket as a metaphor for memory. “When I make the stroke I do not, as a matter of fact, produce something absolutely new and I never merely repeat something old” he wrote in his landmark book Remembering: a Study in Experimental and Social Psychology. Bartlett posited that remembering the past is just like playing a stroke, a cover drive say, in cricket. You can never repeat the stroke exactly, so like a fingerprint or snowflake, no two cover drives are exactly the same, even when played by the same person. Each cover drive is “manufactured” afresh in the new circumstances, the “schemata of the moment and their interrelations”.
summary: A professor of memory argues that Pat Cummins and Usman Khawaja are both telling the truth regarding their recollections of Cape Town. The expert cites English psychologist Frederic Bartlett to explain that human memory is reconstructed each time rather than repeated exactly.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Hamilton denies lack of trust at Ferrari before Las Vegas GP
content:
Lewis Hamilton has denied reports of a lack of trust within his Ferrari team ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The British driver stated that the team is "working on our communication" and emphasized that they are increasingly collaborating effectively, despite instances where he overruled pit calls in two of the last four races.

Hamilton clarified the situation following discussions with teammate Charles Leclerc. The seven-time world champion notably ignored team instructions to pit under the virtual safety car during the October Singapore Grand Prix, a decision made simultaneously with Leclerc.
summary: Lewis Hamilton stated that his Ferrari team is working on communication and is increasingly performing well together. He denied reports of a lack of trust despite overruling pit calls in two of the last four races.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sonay Kartal addresses online abuse and injury recovery
content:
Sonay Kartal, the British No 2 tennis player, has returned to competition after a six‑month absence. She has used her comeback to call for greater action against the vitriolic abuse and threats that players receive online following matches.

Kartal says the abuse has become an unavoidable part of her job. “Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” she told reporters. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.”
summary: British tennis player Sonay Kartal has returned to competition after a six-month injury absence. She states that facing vitriolic online abuse and threats is an unavoidable part of her job as a player.

title: Rep. Nick Begich projected to win second term in Alaska’s at‑large House seat
content: Republican Rep. Nick Begich is projected to win a second term in Alaska’s at‑large House district, according to Decision Desk HQ.  Begich defeated independent Bill Hill—who was backed by Democrats—alongside Democrat Eric Hafner and Libertarian James McDermott in the four‑way general election.  Democrat Matt Schultz suspended his campaign ahead of the election.

content: President Trump told Americans to “relax” and assured them that “everything’s good” regarding recent major outages that have prompted some to stockpile canned food and water. summary: President Trump told Fox News's Jacqui Heinrich in Shenzen, China, that Americans buying and stockpiling canned food and water amid recent major outages should relax and that everything is good. He described the outages as individual events.
